Bitcoin’s [BTC] price slide is accelerating, with the king coin falling below $63,000 amid a new wave of ETF outflows and a broader rotation of capital into the AI sector.

Recent findings suggest that the drop extends a brutal month that has seen roughly $2.58 billion flee U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs since the start of November.

On the 19th of November, Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of $306.50 million, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $209.5 million, roughly 87% of the day’s redemptions.

Recent findings suggest that the price action followed the outflows, as Bitcoin traded near $63,071 at the time of writing, down nearly 3% on the day and hovering at its lowest levels since mid-August. Ethereum fared worse, though, dropping below $1,800 at press time.

In a recent development, another massive factor behind Bitcoin’s fall was noted by the X account Why Markets Move. It stated that right now, investors are seeing more potential in the AI boom and the upcoming Anthropic IPO, compared to crypto.

According to recent reports, for the uninitiated, Anthropic is at the moment targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in its Nasdaq listing, with investors such as Nvidia and Microsoft. This is undoubtedly good news for AI, but not such much for digital assets.

Raj Kamal, founder and CEO of TransFi, told AMBCrypto how policy shifts and macro conditions can crush crypto sentiment. He remarked,.

Recent findings suggest that I think the market read the result as a short-term negative for crypto. Much of the rise in bitcoin and in stablecoin adoption came after the 2024 US election, and investors now expect closer scrutiny of consumer protection, anti-money-laundering rules and the crypto interests of President Trump’s family.

Kamal also outlined how ETF redemptions became another salient point for Bitcoin’s fall.

U.S. Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded about $1.91 billion of net outflows over seven straight sessions from 5 to 13 November. Institutional money began to leave as the price fell, and once Bitcoin went below $70,000, leveraged positions were flushed out.

His outlook was playing out in real life, with November’s cumulative ETF outflows now exceeding $2.5 billion until press time. The CEO ended with a warning.

I don’t think that flushing out is over yet.

On a similar note, stablecoin supply has plunged by roughly $14.28 billion over the past thirty days, signaling a broader drain of dollar liquidity from the crypto ecosystem.

The AI rotation has to simmer down, and regulatory clarity needs to improve for Bitcoin, otherwise its downward spiral will not stop. Therefore, traders have to now watch the $62,000 support level, but a sustained break below will lead BTC to $60,000.

Moving averages on the NEAR chart are diverging and might create conditions for a rapid price recovery, as this directly affects volatility.

According to recent reports, the descending volume in the long term suggests declining power among bears. The descending volume on the upside movement essentially hints at likely price weakening.

It has been revealed that in case of a 200 EMA breakthrough, we are most likely going to see accelerating selling pressure. However, there's a good chance that it won't happen, considering the lack of volatility on the market right now.

Industry observers note that RSI touched around 32 at the bottom and has climbed to around 40 since. RSI is forming a reversal, which is unlikely to contribute to volatility or price whatsoever.

Compared to the rest of the market, Near Protocol is showing somewhat solid performance with a realistic recovery possibility.

The electric Vespa just got better where it actually matters

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that vespa’s electric scooters have never exactly screamed for attention.
  • But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.
  • Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the newly introduced electric Vespa lineup now consists of the Primavera Elettrica, Sprint S Elettrica, and the faster Primavera Tech Elettrica.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that vespa’s electric scooters have never exactly screamed for attention. That’s sort of the point. They look like Vespas, ride like Vespas, and just happen to swap the gasoline engine for a much quieter electric drivetrain.

But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.

Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the newly introduced electric Vespa lineup now consists of the Primavera Elettrica, Sprint S Elettrica, and the faster Primavera Tech Elettrica. And while you’d be forgiven for struggling to spot the differences from across the show floor, there’s a lot more happening underneath.

Recent findings suggest that the biggest upgrade is an entirely new electric motor developed and manufactured in Italy by Vespa parent company Piaggio Group. The motor uses a new modular design intended to improve both performance and efficiency, while also doing away with rare-earth materials.

According to recent reports, on the 45 km/h (28 mph) Primavera and Sprint S models, Vespa claims the newly introduced motor provides stronger acceleration for stop-and-go city riding. Range reaches up to 85 km (53 miles) in Eco mode.

It has been revealed that but perhaps the biggest practical improvement is the new removable battery. Being able to pull the battery out of the scooter and carry it inside for charging makes a massive difference for urban riders who don’t have access to a garage or dedicated charging spot – exactly the kind of riders Vespa is targeting.

It has been revealed that the Primavera Tech is where things get a little faster. This version is homologated as a motorcycle rather than a moped in Europe and reaches 67 km/h (42 mph). That’s still not terribly fast, but the electric Vespa line has never been known for its top speed.

Its range has increased by 12.5% thanks to the newly introduced motor and Vehicle Management System, reaching 90 km (56 miles) on the WMTC cycle or up to 100 km (62 miles) in Eco mode.

Industry observers note that there’s also a fresh charger that Vespa indicates reduces energy consumption from the wall by 17%, with a 0-80% charge taking around 2.5 hours. A new Maintenance mode is designed to protect the battery during longer periods when the scooter isn’t being ridden.

In a recent development, vespa is clearly only really interested in selling their gas models, which come in 50cc, 125cc, & 310cc classes. And the only reason anyone would get a 50cc is if they didn't want to bother to get an actual motorcycle license in some jurisdictions. The electrics are nearly as expensive as the 310s but even the "faster" model only has the power equivalent of about 70cc's. At least the battery in the faster model is now a decent 4.2 kwh, though that one I believe is not removable. Hey I'm actually a Vespa lover I have a 200cc. They are beautiful quality machines, and I don't mind the price premium. But the electrics are quite disappointing, especially for the money. If they had a true 125cc equivalent I would be first in line at the showroom. Very disappointing in that a stouter motor really wouldn't cost them much more at all.

The Primavera Tech also gets the technological bells and whistles you’d expect from the flagship version, including a 5-inch TFT display, keyless operation, navigation through Vespa’s smartphone connectivity system, and remote seat unlocking.

Perhaps the most Vespa thing about the whole update is how little of it you can actually see.

Sources indicate that the firm hasn’t tried to turn its electric scooters into rolling science-fiction props. They’re still unmistakably Vespas, complete with the same classic styling that has defined the brand for generations. They just happen to have a much more interesting electric drivetrain hiding underneath now.

Of course, they also carry some very Vespa pricing. While we don’t have word on the updated pricing for the new models, the outgoing Primavera Elettrica 70 RED was priced at $8,299 in the US. So don’t expect these models to come cheap.

Veteran commodity trader Peter Brandt has provided yet another bearish outlook for the world's largest cryptocurrency, arguing that the crypto asset could see much more misery if its historical market trends play out.

In a recent development, bitcoin Bitcoin Every bull market phase in BTC's history has ended with at least a 75% correction of the previous parabolic bull trend. Could this be what's happening in Bitcoin? https://t.co/PVXJpetSyO.

Brandt's latest doomsday prediction comes at a time when Bitcoin is still trying to recover from its biggest sell-off to date, which has wiped out close to half of its market value from its October 2025 peak.

The trader's latest post on X highlights a pattern he has found throughout Bitcoin's price history: previous bull runs have always ended with devastating market corrections.

"Every bull market phase in the history of BTC has ended with at least a 75% correction of the prior parabolic bull trend," Brandt's X post reads.

Continuing his warning, Brandt raised an alarming question: "Is this what is happening with Bitcoin?".

Industry observers note that the trading veteran has not put a number on the possible crash. But his words point toward the possibility that the current drop in Bitcoin might be part of a larger correction and not just a temporary dip.

A look at Bitcoin's historical crashes could paint a scary picture.

Bitcoin has a history of sharp corrections following major bull runs.

For example, the crypto asset dropped by around 84% from its December 2017 high to its December 2018 low. Another example of such a deep price correction can be found in the 2022 bear market, when BTC saw a drop of around 77% from its November 2021 all-time high.

These historic crashes have shown the extreme losses that Bitcoin investors have faced during such market corrections.

At the time of writing on Nov. 20, Bitcoin is right now trading at around $62,000, which is almost 51% below its October 2025 all-time high.

If it were to undergo a 75% price correction from its all-time high, then it would drop to around $31,550.

But it's worth mentioning that Brandt referred to a correction of the prior parabolic bull trend, which may not be the same as a 75% correction from the peak.

Interestingly enough, this is not the first time the trader has warned about an even darker future for Bitcoin's price.

Sources indicate that earlier, on Nov. 15, Brandt shared a weekly BTC chart showing a potential head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern that usually signals a bearish reversal.

According to Brandt, if the pattern is confirmed, there's a chance that Bitcoin could never revisit its previous all-time high in his lifetime.

Sources indicate that the chart he shared also indicates an vital zone between $60,000 and $65,000. A confirmed breakdown below this zone could further strengthen the bearish outlook.

Moreover, there is still plenty of selling pressure in the crypto market. The latest revision from Lookonchain on Nov. 19 revealed that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had seen net outflows of around $975 million over the past seven days. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, on the 19th of November, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse mentioned in an interview with CNBC that the recent crypto market sell-off is a result of capital rotating into IPOs like Anthropic. However, he does expect the markets to rebound once the listing is complete.

Still on-chain data for XRP suggests that despite on-chain indicators looking bullish, the altcoin is struggling to move beyond the $1 psychological level.

Garlinghouse argued that the recent bloodbath across digital assets is less about a fundamental collapse in crypto and more about investors shifting funds to chase the AI boom.

He pointed to a previous sell-off in the market, acknowledging,.

According to recent reports, we also saw a sell-off very similar when SpaceX went public. What happens is… people are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market in crypto, including Bitcoin and XRP, and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Athropic IPO… What we saw after the SpaceX IPO is a rally in the crypto market.

He believes that the same story will play out with the Anthropic IPO too.

Garlinghouse’s bullish thesis does have a solid footing. Most notably, CryptoQuant’s data demonstrates that the XRP Exchange Reserve on Binance has been declining over the last thirty days.

In late October 2026, Binance held roughly 2.7 billion XRP, but the figure dropped to 2.47 billion XRP as of the 19th of November.

When Exchange Reserve falls, it typically signals that investors are moving coins to self-custody, reducing the immediate supply available for selling.

Industry observers note that despite the tightening supply on exchanges, XRP’s price action remains volatile. At press time, XRP was trading at $0.9834, down 1.4% in the last 24 hours.

The chart further revealed a market struggling to find firm footing. XRP managed to hold above $1 during November 12-14 before a steep drop dragged it down to the $0.90 region.

The last 24 hours saw the asset sail briefly above $1 but faced an immediate rejection, slumping back into the high $0.90s.

As XRP remains in a tug-of-war between falling exchange reserves and repeated price rejections at $1.00, investors are uncertain about its next direction.

According to recent reports, if Garlinghouse is correct and digital assets do rally after the Anthropic IPO, the rotation will easily cause prices to soar beyond $1. However, until that macroeconomic shift occurs, XRP holders appear content to move their coins off exchanges and wait out the storm.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • After introducing the upcoming and improved bZ (formerly the bZ4X) in late 2025, the electric SUV promptly became one of the most popular EVs in the US.
  • In the first nine months of 2026, it was the fourth-best-selling electric vehicle, behind the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that toyota now offers three fully electric SUVs: the bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland. Here’s how they stack up.

After introducing the upcoming and improved bZ (formerly the bZ4X) in late 2025, the electric SUV promptly became one of the most popular EVs in the US.

In the first nine months of 2026, it was the fourth-best-selling electric vehicle, behind the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.

With two additional electric SUVs now on sale, the CH-R and bZ Woodland, Toyota has suddenly become one of America’s top-selling EV brands.

Its EV sales have nearly tripled this year. According to Cox Automotive, Toyota ranked as the third most popular EV brand behind Tesla and Rivian in the third quarter.

Toyota offers three distinct electric vehicles: the 2027 bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland, each designed for different lifestyles, so which one is the best fit for you?

According to recent reports, after launching the updated model last year, the 2027 bZ starts at $34,980. With the $1,595 delivery fee, the starting price is $36,576.

In a recent development, that’s for the standard 2027 Toyota bZ XLE FWD with an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 236 miles. For longer range, you can upgrade to the FWD Plus model, which offers up to 314 miles and starts at $37,980 (excluding the delivery fee).

The Toyota bZ is available in XLE and Limited grades, with front- or all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrains.

Two battery options are offered: The 57.7 kWh battery on the standard XLE FWD provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 236 miles, while the larger 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 288 miles of range on the XLE AWD and 314 miles on the XLE FWD Plus model.

FWD models produce either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models deliver a combined 338 hp.

The 2027 bZ also has a built-in NACS port, so you can use Tesla Superchargers without needing a separate adapter. Toyota said it takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

Inside, the 2027 bZ features Toyota’s updated cabin design. The setup features a 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and a upcoming 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The bZ is essentially designed as an everyday driver with a long driving range, modern tech, and available AWD.

It has been revealed that for those looking for a bigger, more rugged option, the 2027 bZ Woodland may be a better fit. The Woodland is 6″ longer than the standard bZ and comes with standard AWD.

The longer body opens up more interior space, with up to 74.3 cubic feet of storage compared to the bZ with up to 67.1 cubic feet.

Unlike the bZ, the Woodland model has a standard AWD powertrain with Toyota’s X-Mode control system.

The setup delivers a combined 375 horsepower, 37 hp more than the standard bZ, making it Toyota’s most powerful EV at the moment.

It also adopts a more commanding, upright stance with 8.3″ of ground clearance and 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Although it uses the same 74.7 kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland’s EPA-estimated range drops to 281 miles because of the added weight and power. Upgrading to the optional all-terrain tires sacrifices even more range, with up to 260 miles.

In a recent development, like the bZ, the Woodland also has a built- in NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes around 30 minutes.

Inside, the bZ Woodland features the same 7″ LCD customizable Multi Information Display (MID) and 14″ Toyota Audio Multimedia display screen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380. All variants include standard roof rails, Dual Qi-capable wireless device chargers, heated front seats and steering wheel, and Digital Key capabilities.

Last, but not least, the C-HR is a smaller, sporty, coupe-like electric SUV. The 2027 Toyota C-HR starts at $37,080, or $2,100 more than the standard bZ.

It has been revealed that it’s about 6.7″ shorter than the bZ, with a smaller wheelbase, but also comes with standard AWD. The dual-motor AWD setup delivers a combined 338 hp, not quite as much as the bigger, more powerful Woodland.

The C-HR is available exclusively with the 74.7 kWh battery, which provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 287 miles for the SE grade with 18″ wheels.

Upgrading to 20″ wheels adds a street-ready look but offers slightly less EPA range, with up to 273 miles.

The coupe-like design adds a sleek look and opens up interior space, with up to 59.5 cubic feet of rear cargo space when the rear seats are folded. That’s slightly more than the bZ, which offers up to 56.9 cubic feet.

Inside, the C-HR features the same setup as its other EVs, including a 7″ slim driver’s display and 14″ central infotainment screen.

According to recent reports, like Toyota’s other electric SUVs, the C-HR has a native NACS port. Charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes about 30 minutes.

These are all basically the same small vehicles. I did not fit in any of them (6’ 2”) it is so frustrating to have less than 300 miles of range on AWD versions that are supposed to be better models.

According to recent reports, it is 2026 over a decade since EVs arrived and over 5 years after the Tesla Model Y with practically zero competition almost at same price (Rivian R2 may be next year when affordable versions ship.) BMW, Mercedes and Volvo need $10k more. Hyundai has kept EV5 out of USA.

It is almost like none of the Legacy automakers want any SUV that can compete on price.

The 2027 Toyota C-HR EV is available in two trims: SE and XSE. Standard features include two wireless Qi phone chargers, low-profile roof rails, Fabric/SofTex-trimmed seating, heated front seats and steering wheel, Toyota Safety Sense 3.0, and a power liftgate.

Which Toyota electric SUV would you choose? The bZ, C-HR, or bZ Woodland? Or would you choose another EV? Let us know your pick in the comments. Next year, Toyota will add the Highland EV, its first three-row electric SUV.

Noted economist and longtime Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff has sounded the alarm about an upcoming financial apocalypse, warning that the crisis could be worse than the historic 2008 market crash.

Sources indicate that on Nov. 20, Peter Schiff shared a series of troubling X posts warning about the potential for significant losses in the U.S. stock market, real estate, and cryptocurrencies amid escalating financial system stress.

The economist shared a video with a very alarming headline: "The Next Crash Will Be Worse Than 2008.".

In one of his most recent posts on X, Schiff argued that the recent gold price downtrend might signal a grim outlook for other key asset classes.

"It's probably a bad sign that gold is falling this much. It probably means that the stock and real estate markets are going to fall even more in percentage terms," Schiff cautioned.

Sources indicate that according to Peter Schiff, gold's recent price behavior could be signaling deflation. As a result, this might lead to a more severe financial crisis.

However, Peter Schiff is convinced that the Federal Reserve will step in to prevent this financial apocalypse.

"Gold is signaling deflation. But asset deflation would bust the government and the banking system, so the Fed will pivot to avoid it," the economist explained.

Simply put, Schiff assumes that the Federal Reserve will pivot and introduce monetary stimulus to prevent a financial meltdown.

According to recent reports, in another startling prediction, the economist warned that the U.S. stock market might wipe out all its gains since President Donald Trump took office.

"There's a good chance that the U.S. stock market is about to give back all the gains since Trump took office," the economist predicted.

He also warned that there might be a recession. As a result, Trump will likely point to Democrats and their wins in the recent midterm elections as the reason for this recession.

Interestingly enough, Peter Schiff's bearish outlook also applies to Bitcoin (BTC), which has already suffered significant losses amid the overall market crash.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 18, Peter Schiff shared several alarming market indicators. According to his data, the Nasdaq has dropped 12.25%. AI infrastructure firm CoreWeave has plummeted 64%.

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has plunged 33.5% from its 2026 peak.

It has been revealed that additionally, the economist noted that the U.S. housing market index had dropped to 25, its lowest level since 2012. This highlights that the economic concerns go well beyond AI stocks.

"Still think this is just about AI?" he asked.

Home » Altcoins » XRP & XLM Hit Closest To ‘Value Area’ Among Major-Caps.

These two major-cap altcoin peers are hitting close to historically-undervalued territory: a highly-awaited bottom sign?

French analyst EGRAG compared the 4-hour charts of XRP, Ethereum, Hedera, Bitcoin, Solana, and Stellar to assess which assets are showing relative strength after recent lows.

The mainstream French crypto chart analyst’s review centers on price reaction, volume-profile location, and the distance remaining to each coin’s Value Area Low (VAL).

In a recent development, on the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better. Unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case. Especially for those in the XRP and Solana markets.

In a recent development, both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching plans to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them. It cited no specific reason in its filings with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission for these new plans.

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”.

In a recent development, the registration documents for both these ETFs were filed way back in October 2025. That’s over a year ago. As recently as 06 November, the Trust had submitted an extension. This would have allowed the registrations to become effective by 06 December.

It has been revealed that however, an important distinction must be made here. It must be pointed out that the ETFs Roundhill was planning to launch were income-focused products. These ETFs would have relied on income generated by trading Options linked to existing crypto prodcuts.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

Industry observers note that consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being introduced in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

These numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

In a recent development, this, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

The new Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past.

Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan, including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.

The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ uses a 122 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 467 miles.

Recent findings suggest that while that’s already impressive, the electric sedan will likely go even farther in everyday driving conditions. During Edmunds recent EV Range Test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ drove a whopping 539 miles without stopping to charge.

It has been revealed that the EQS beat its own EPA estimate by 72 miles and is now the longest-range electric sedan Edmunds has ever tested, beating the Lucid Air, the first EV to break the 500-mile mark. The only EV that has it beat is the Cadillac Escalade IQ, which managed 558 miles from its massive 205 kWh battery.

During the test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ was also more efficient than its official numbers suggest.

In a recent development, the fresh EQS used 29.6 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 28 kWh per 100 miles. In comparison, the 2025 Mercedes EQS 450+ covered 464 miles and used 34 kWh per 100 miles during the same test, so the improvements are considerable.

Edmunds observed a peak charging rate of 350 kW, in line with Mercedes’ estimates, while it sustained an average of 222 kW throughout the session.

Both beat the older EQS, which reached a peak charge rate of 208 kW and sustained an average of 175 kW.

The fresh Mercedes EQS 450+ added 825 miles of range in an hour, and 100 miles in just over 7 minutes, nearly twice the speed of the 2025MY.

It has been revealed that the Edmunds EV Range Test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions. It includes 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

How much is too much? 539 miles on a single charge is impressive, but do you need it? In a recent “nationally representative” survey, BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.

Sources indicate that the study showed that 73% consider 25, 50, or 75 miles enough to cover their daily driving. However, 42% said they would require at least 300 miles of range before they would consider an EV.

If you have access to a home charger, nothing beats waking up with a full charge every day. Meanwhile, public charging continues to improve, giving EV drivers more reliable options on longer trips.

It has been revealed that faster charging also helps. Another 53% remarked they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in around 10 minutes.

In the same Edmunds EV Range Test last week, the new 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive drove 436 miles on a single charge, exceeding its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles. It also used 28.3 kWh per 100 miles during the test, beating its official EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles.

I'm really glad to see more articles like this and people talking more about efficiency. It's not just about bigger batteries and range. It needs to be about smaller batteries plus great efficiency giving that same range. We need to do this with more efficient designs, more sedans and lighter vehicles.

The new 2027 Volvo EX60 drove 352 miles while the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric covered 392 miles during the same test.

Industry observers note that one thing is certain: electric vehicles are becoming more efficient, enabling longer driving ranges and faster charging times. As battery tech advances, EVs will drive farther and charge faster, while safety and performance will continue to improve.

It has been revealed that if you struggle with bumps and irritation, an electric razor might be your new best friend. Of course, you still need to make sure you use that electric razor properly. Dermatologists say you should follow the below best practices for a smooth shave every time.

According to recent reports, make sure your skin is well hydrated before shaving because using an electric razor over dry, irritated skin can make matters worse, says dermatologist Joshua Zeichner, MD. Dr. Robinson adds that you should also use a gentle cleanser prior to shaving. And, avoid fragrance or products known to cause irritation immediately before and after shaving, she says.

Recent findings suggest that and please, do so in the direction of the hair growth, says Dr. Zeichner. Repeated strokes over the same area increase the likelihood of irritation and ingrown hairs.

Recent findings suggest that hydration is key. "I advise patients that they do not need a dedicated post-shave or aftercare lotion—a gentle moisturizer is just fine in these areas," indicates Dr. Robinson, who likes light, fragrance-free formulas. Aside from that, Dr. Robinson recommends making sure you follow any specific instructions on the product package—in other words, you should actually read the directions.

It has been revealed that at the end of the day, everyone's going to have their personal preference, and it's not worth, ahem, splitting hairs if you prefer one type of razor over another. That being said, if your skin is prone to irritation, it might be time to ditch the traditional razor. With an electric razor, you’re not scraping against the skin really hard like a traditional razor does, notes dermatologist Cameron Rokhsar, MD. This means that you won't see a lot of the cuts and burns that sometimes result from a manual blade, says Dr. Rokhsar. There are also areas of the body that might be better suited to shave with an electric razor. "Most women's electric razors are designed for our curvy areas," says Dr. Ploch. "I prefer electric razors around the ankles because manual razors cut this area easily.".

In a recent development, keeping your electric razor clean is incredibly notable, says Dr. Rokhsar. Many derms will recommend changing a manual razor every time you shave, but you can't do that with an electric one, which makes running the blades under warm water after use a crucial step. This will keep it free of hair, shaving cream, and other residues.

According to recent reports, dr. Rokhsar also recommends swiping over the blades and the outside of the razor with a rubbing alcohol-soaked cotton ball regularly. "Especially if it sits in your bathroom moisture, bacteria will accumulate on the blades," he says. "It's an easy entry point for bacteria to go down the hair follicle." That's a big no-no if you want to stay free of irritation or infection.

Sources indicate that our team of editors follow Dr. Rokhsar's advice and it hasn't led us astray. And despite evaluating some of these razors for close to a year, we are pleased that we haven't noticed any rusting after using the alcohol-soaked cotton ball.

Sources indicate that another tip is to actually read and follow the maintenance instructions of your device. (Admittedly, we threw ours away since we've been using these for several months and like to keep the limited space of our beauty closet as streamlined as possible.) You can also prioritize using devices like the Philips Series 5000 Electric Facial Hair Remover that's easy to clean, as the head can easily be removed so you can dump shaved hair and dead skin cells straight into the garbage.

In a recent development, "Rich Dad Poor Dad" author Robert Kiyosaki wrote on X on Nov. 20 that he is "most excited about Bitcoin's crash" and is "waiting to buy more." On the same day, Bitcoin was trading at $61,666, more than 50% below its October 2025 peak of about $126,000.

Gold fell 1.24% to $3,579 an ounce, and silver lost 0.95% to $42.42, according to TradingView data. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% on the same day.

According to recent reports, kiyosaki started his post with a question. "CRASH: Good or Bad? Gold, silver, Bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy?" he wrote.

According to Kiyosaki, the reasons include "incompetence in FED, Banks, and Bond markets." He also wrote that America's debt is "only to grow bigger" as "Banksters steal our wealth via their system legally.".

The author pointed to Bitcoin's fixed supply. There will be only 21 million BTC in total, and about 20 million coins have already been mined, Kiyosaki wrote. "As far as I know, there has never been a 'money' such as Bitcoin ever before," he added.

"With price of Bitcoin crashing, I can't wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a 'nothing burger'…. or the best money I've ever spent," Kiyosaki wrote.

In late August, Kiyosaki said on podcasts that he owed creditors $1.2 billion. His ex-wife and business partner, Kim Kiyosaki, later said that the figure covered the loans of a partnership that owns about 1,500 rental units. "We have a lot of apartment houses with our partners," she said.

According to Kim Kiyosaki, Robert Kiyosaki's own share of the debt is $30 million to $60 million. Each of their real estate investments is held in a separate LLC. Robert Kiyosaki also commented on the debt at the time. "If it all comes to hell, you can talk to my attorney," he noted.

In 2012, Kiyosaki's company Rich Global LLC filed for bankruptcy after a court ordered it to pay about $24 million.

PlugShare is giving its EV charging app a massive overhaul. Version 8.0 arrives worldwide for iPhone on November 10, with dark mode, a trip planner that shows how far apart charging stops are, and a rebuilt Apple Watch app that can point you to a charger compatible with your EV.

In a recent development, dark mode was one of the most-requested features from PlugShare consumers. It works across the app and follows your iPhone’s settings, so if your phone switches to dark mode at sunset, your charging map will, too.

The app also adapts its layout to the iPhone Duo’s different screens and folded positions.

The rebuilt Watch app lists nearby charging stations with distances and directions. It uses the filters you’ve set on your iPhone, so if you’ve filtered for plugs that fit your EV, that carries over to your wrist.

In a recent development, tap a station and you’ll see its PlugScore, the network that runs it, a small map, and which plugs it has, including NACS, CCS, CHAdeMO, or J1772. The list refreshes when you raise your wrist and open the app. You can also add a shortcut to a round or corner slot on your watch face.

In a recent development, the iPhone update is rolling out through the App Store. PlugShare notes Android users will get dark mode and a redesign based on Google’s Material 3 in early 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that what started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide.
  • The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that what started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into fresh industries.

It has been revealed that the group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop new services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

It has been revealed that in 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

According to recent reports, W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each firm can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

Sources indicate that in 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

In a recent development, trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

In a recent development, whiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT launched a dedicated platform for users in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The firm also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into latest products and services.

It has been revealed that “Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million users. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making newly introduced technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” mentioned Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Recent findings suggest that looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300.

Three separate market pressures just collided—pushing BTC to a level not seen since July.

Bitcoin plunged 4.35% over the past 24 hours, falling to $61,300 — its lowest level since early July — as a global sell-off in AI stocks, heavy withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs and a wave of forced liquidations sent shockwaves through crypto markets.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin was struggling to stay above $61,500, putting it on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

According to recent reports, this drop wasn’t triggered by a single event. Instead, several pressures hit the market at once: growing concerns over AI valuations, institutional investors pulling money out of Bitcoin ETFs, and leveraged traders being forced to close their positions as prices fell.

The broader pullback was driven by a retreat from riskier assets as investors questioned lofty AI valuations.

Industry observers note that on Thursday, November 19, AI firm Anthropic made its highly anticipated debut on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50 against an IPO price of $83, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion. However, the successful IPO failed to lift sentiment across the technology sector.

As Anthropic began trading, Bitcoin fell from around $62,700 to $62,250 within roughly 30 minutes, while broader Nasdaq losses accelerated.

By the end of the session, the Nasdaq was down 2.3%, the S&P 500 had fallen 2%, and the Dow Jones lost 2.2%.

The sell-off spread to Asia, where South Korea’s KOSPI dropped approximately 5%, triggering a temporary restriction on automated selling.

Institutional demand for Bitcoin is also showing signs of weakening, adding further pressure to an already struggling market.

According to recent reports, according to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.19 million in net outflows on November 19, marking the largest single-day withdrawal of the month.

With the exception of a modest $8 million inflow on November 5, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have faced nearly two weeks of persistent capital withdrawals, signaling a significant pullback in institutional demand.

As spot prices broke below key support levels, leveraged derivatives traders fueled a cascade of forced selling.

It has been revealed that coinGlass data highlights $697.35 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours. About $600M came from long positions, and $201.25M of the total was Bitcoin longs.

According to market analyst Axel Adler Jr., Bitcoin remains under significant bearish pressure, with short-term investors sitting on substantial unrealized losses. Bitcoin is currently trading 15.7% below the average cost basis of recent buyers and has remained below that level for 12 consecutive days.

Until BTC reclaims the short-term holder cost basis and U.S. spot ETF flows flip back into positive territory, an analyst warns that the broader market correction isn’t over yet.

Bitcoin’s slide alongside AI stocks underscores how tightly crypto still tracks risk appetite in traditional markets. Continued ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations are likely to keep pressure on prices until broader market sentiment stabilizes.

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the organization.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it introduced its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data indicates that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

The latest funding round for the driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform developer was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from other existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners. Humble said it will use the funding for customer pilots, testing and validation, and early manufacturing.

Industry observers note that “We’ve spent years proving that a truck can drive itself,” explains Humble Robotics founder and CEO, Eyal Cohen. “The harder question is how to make autonomy something a freight operator can depend on every day.”.

According to recent reports, we originally covered the Humble Hauler back in May. You can check out the original article, below, then let us know what you think of the organization’s prospects in the comments.

The startup that dares to ask, “Why does the Macbook driving my freight around need a whole cab?” just showed off a fully driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform designed to handle containerized cargo more efficiently than ever.

Sources indicate that instead of looking at the tractor and asking how to make it work without a driver, Humble looked at the trailer, itself, redesigning the container chassis as a vehicle from the ground up. The end result isn’t just an autonomous solution, it’s an overall lighter platform without a cab that saves shippers the weight of a sleeper cab, a day cab, or the truck at all.

The Humble approach is said to improve payload efficiency of shipping containers, and intended for dock-to-dock operation.

It has been revealed that “I have dedicated my career to building electric and autonomous vehicle technology,” explains Eyal Cohen, Humble Robotics’ founder and CEO. “For the first time, freight can be fully automated all the way to the loading dock. We are making freight sustainable, safe and efficient in a way no one thought was possible. And we’re doing it with an exceptional team of industry veterans and AV experts.”.

Emerging from stealth after a $24 million funding round, Humble claims to have completed its first Humble Hauler prototype in less than six months – and they’ll soon be ready to begin autonomous testing in pilot programs with a number of logistics partners.

The vehicle uses a combination of cameras, lidar, and radar for 360-degree awareness (unhindered by seeing around a cab), and uses vision-language-action models to help the system respond to new scenarios.

Sources indicate that thanks to superior battery tech, a maturing global charging infrastructure, and a permanently damaged MidEast oil supply, there’s never been a better time to be an EV startup. Humble is hitting all the electric trailer buzzwords, too, while also touting the fact that the electric powertrain can reduce a organization’s to volatile fuel prices even as it helps produce other cost benefits like lower maintenance costs.

Sources indicate that there is a reason why the transportation industry developed separate cabs and trailers. Trailers can be loaded or unloaded for days and are much less expensive than trucks that serve both purposes in one piece. That allows the more expensive piece of the transport puzzle to be used more and allows the trailer to be loaded and unloaded while the cab is elsewhere working or in the shop. Query whether the savings they cite will surpass the costs of not having the flexibility of a cab and trailer design.

And if a robot like this can deliver on its promises without the baked-in inefficiencies of humanoids, they might be one step closer to provide that the most efficient solution to a problem is rarely a general one, and even rarer is it a solution that looks like a human.

Sources indicate that the Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

According to recent reports, on 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Sources indicate that some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and Latest York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

In a recent development, $2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

It has been revealed that according to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

Sources indicate that however, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

According to recent reports, will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Recent findings suggest that is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

Three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

Recent findings suggest that XRPScan data indicates that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain.".

Industry observers note that the model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool highlighted the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan says on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed.".

In a recent development, standard Chartered noted Nov. 19 that eligible clients can now transfer tokenized deposits, bank balances recorded on a digital ledger, between Singapore and Hong Kong in near real time.

That gives corporate treasury teams a way to shift cash between entities in the same group on the bank’s own blockchain.

Meanwhile, a separate trial with OCBC and StraitsX tested payments across two banks’ networks.

The bank’s Singapore expansion covers treasury and investment transactions that use commercial bank deposits. Standard Chartered listed the Singapore dollar, Hong Kong dollar, US dollar, euro, offshore Chinese yuan and British pound among the supported currencies.

It named corporate treasurers, banks, investment platforms, and digital asset businesses as potential people, but detailed eligibility criteria and operating hours for the route remain unspecified.

The bank disclosed round-the-clock settlement when it released its Hong Kong service Nov. 2. That schedule applies to tokenized deposit transactions settled between participating banks in central bank money through the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s EnsembleTX infrastructure.

It has been revealed that on Nov. 19, Standard Chartered, Singapore bank OCBC and payment infrastructure provider StraitsX said they had completed a controlled trial under the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s BLOOM initiative.

The trial completed US dollar payments across the banks’ separate deposit networks outside conventional cutoffs. Participants said the test showed how payments could move within minutes, including compliance checks, liquidity checks, and settlement.

The trial partners, StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered, explain that each tokenized deposit remains a claim on the bank that issued it. Banks can use different platforms and standards for their deposits, so interbank payments need a way to coordinate settlement across those systems.

Industry observers note that standard Chartered opened a transfer route for eligible clients between Singapore and Hong Kong. A separate trial tested US dollar payments between two banks’ deposit networks.

Industry observers note that A payment across two deposit networks needs a way to coordinate settlement. Each deposit remains a claim on its issuing bank.

Standard Chartered’s release gives no schedule for the live route. The trial partners say a commercial service remains subject to approvals and operational assessments.

The diagram compares the live transfer path described by Standard Chartered with the shared settlement arrangement described by StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered. Connectors represent network relationships.

Standard Chartered’s release gives no schedule for the live route. The trial partners say a commercial service remains subject to approvals and operational assessments.

StraitsX coordinated payment instructions and transaction details and helped with screening and settlement. The shared infrastructure handled the payment process across both networks, from initiation to confirmation.

The partners reported that this setup reduced the need for bilateral prefunding, where banks set aside money in advance to cover payments.

A commercial service based on the trial would still depend on regulatory engagement, participant approval, legal documentation, and operational risk assessments, the partners stated. They also flagged settlement finality, meaning when a payment becomes irrevocable.

Banks would need to work out who is responsible for each step, how to screen for financial crime and how to keep enough funds available for payments to settle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Honda has been getting increasingly serious about electric motorcycles, but if you want to see just how weird the tech giant thinks the future could get, take a look at the Honda EV Outlier Concept.

According to recent reports, I got a chance to see the wild-looking machine in person at EICMA in Milan, where it looked like almost nothing else on the show floor. And that’s exactly the point.

Industry observers note that the EV Outlier Concept originally debuted at last year’s Japan Mobility Show as Honda’s attempt to imagine an electric motorcycle that isn’t simply a conventional motorcycle with the engine swapped for a battery and motor. In fact, Honda describes the concept as looking toward the future of electric motorcycles beyond 2030.

The result is certainly unconventional.

This ain’t your grandpa’s SuperCub.

It has been revealed that instead of a centrally mounted motor driving the rear wheel, the EV Outlier uses motors inside both wheels, giving it all-wheel drive and allowing Honda’s designers to completely rethink the rest of the motorcycle’s layout. The battery is housed in that large central black body, while the rider sits extremely low and behind it.

Honda describes the design philosophy with three words: “Gliding, Ecstasy, and Low.” The first refers to the smooth, nearly silent feeling of electric propulsion, while the second describes the instant acceleration and massive torque available from independently controlled front and rear motors. “Low” is more literal: Honda deliberately dropped the rider’s seating and eye position to create an entirely different sensation from a conventional motorcycle.

There’s even a bucket-style backrest designed to support the rider under hard acceleration and let the rider pivot through corners around their hips.

Cool and fun for Honda engineers to play with, but it seems a massive no for reality, or at least a different road reality then mine.

Recent findings suggest that emergency tight swerves for accident avoidance? Nope, gone. Seeing even less of the road, even without a car in front of you, due to being so low? Not good for me nor the deer I don't avoid due to seeing it too late.

Unsprung mass due to hub motors - lots of literature on that topic, so I'll leave that alone.

Up front, traditional mirrors are replaced by cameras, while a wide digital cockpit can display things like lean angle, riding modes, front motor torque adjustment, and what the two wheels are doing in real time.

Industry observers note that will Honda actually build this thing? Almost certainly not exactly as you see it here. That’s what concepts are for.

It has been revealed that but the EV Outlier is still interesting as a statement of intent. Honda is obviously still playing around with the freedom that electric drivetrains offer, and the organization is asking what motorcycles could become once designers no longer have to work around engines, fuel tanks, transmissions, and traditional drivetrains.

And judging by what I saw at EICMA, Honda’s answer could get pretty wild.

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia.

Tokenized Take-Two shares saw a massive 24-hour trading spike as on-chain markets attract Washington scrutiny.

The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI didn’t just break gaming records—it briefly turned publisher Take-Two Interactive into the hottest stock on the blockchain, outselling even AI giant Nvidia.

On November 18, decentralized exchange (DEX) trading volume for tokenized Take-Two shares (TTWO) exploded by 578%, jumping from $36.8 million to $249.5 million in a single day, according to Token Terminal data.

That was roughly 2.8 times the $88.1 million traded in tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) shares over the same 24-hour window, accounting for 42% of all on-chain stock trading.

Nearly all of the action, roughly $239 million, or 96% of total volume, happened on Solana via Backpack Securities, a subsidiary of crypto exchange Backpack. Introduced earlier this year, the token is designed to be backed 1:1 by real Take-Two shares held in custody.

Traditional Wall Street traders saw a much calmer reaction: Take-Two’s Nasdaq shares rose 6.2% to close at $216.61 on launch day before pulling back 3.7% to $208.65 the next session.

Despite Take-Two’s one-day viral spike, Nvidia remains the undisputed heavyweight of tokenized equities, boasting a $399.4 million market cap and $2 billion in 30-day trading volume (compared to Take-Two’s $808.1 million).

Overall, tokenized public stocks on Solana have nearly doubled since late October to reach $1.22 billion.

Recent findings suggest that that rapid growth is drawing fresh scrutiny in Washington. On November 16, four Democratic senators sent a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) questioning how its newly introduced exemption for tokenized securities would address investor protection and anti-money laundering requirements.

The issue also surfaced during the November 19 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Kristin Johnson, President Donald Trump’s nominee for the SEC. Johnson indicated that exemptions covering tokenized stocks should eventually be formalized through rules following a public comment period.

The TTWO spike shows tokenized stocks can attract event-driven trading on-chain, comparable to some of the largest names in the segment. It also coincides with growing regulatory scrutiny of how tokenized stocks are supervised.

In fact, on Hyperliquid itself, the action is only heating up now.

On Wednesday, Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid to its Alert List. The problem cited was that they don’t hold a licence to operate in the city.

Recent findings suggest that the regulator’s entry covers two names; Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong. It also shared the exchange’s trading website. It is believed that the platform may be serving Hong Kong users, presenting itself as a local operator, or pitching its services to people in the city.

With this addition, the SFC’s list of suspicious crypto trading platforms has grown to 69 names now. At the time of writing, Hyperliquid hadn’t commented on the development.

Back in June, Singapore’s central bank placed Hyperliquid on its Investor Alert List which flags firms people might wrongly assume are regulated there. At the time, Hyperliquid’s response was simple — it never noted it had a Singapore licence.

Now, there are two Asian financial hubs keeping an eye on the exchange.

While Hong Kong was flagging Hyperliquid, traders on the platform were busy betting on Anthropic.

On 18th November, the number of traders holding long positions on Anthropic perps hit a record 5,567.

Industry observers note that A week ago, that figure was 2,926; nearly doubling in seven days. There were 1,996 short holders, with the same hinting at 2.8 longs for every short.

In a recent development, most of that action was on Trade[XYZ]’s ANT market. According to Token Terminal, this alone accounted for 4,190 long holders,.

One caveat, though. These numbers count traders, not the size of their bets. And since the data adds up three markets, anyone trading on two of them gets counted twice.

Not great, but not terrible either.

It has been revealed that the altcoin was trading at $67.66, at press time, following a hike of just 1% in the last 24 hours. Its price was still a long way from its late-October levels when it briefly climbed above $95. Since then, it’s been mostly downhill for the crypto.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that diesel-electric locomotives have been barreling along America’s wide-open spaces for generations, and the century-old combination of highly efficient diesel engines spinning up generators to power high-torque electric motors has proven tough to beat. Now, Caterpillar is putting that century-old concept to work underground. Meet the CAT R3200 XE LHD.

Recent findings suggest that one of the many hard-working machines moving chunks of Earth under your feet, an LHD (load, haul, and dump) machine is essentially a massive underground wheel loader designed to scoop up blasted rock, haul it through narrow mine tunnels, then dump it into trucks or ore passes. Built low and wide to fit in the tunnels, LHDs are workhorses of underground mining operations – and the new R3200 XE is CAT’s biggest yet, with a 25 ton payload and electric drive.

Before we get into the machine’s specs (the few that we have, anyway), I want to make sure understand that large-scale mining operations use obscene amounts of fuel, and a swing in site efficiency of just 1-2% can mean a huge difference in the bottom line – and fuel prices were up 27.4% (!) in August alone.

Keep the staggering weight of what that kind of fuel cost can mean to a fleet that buys fuel by the literal truckload as you read the rest of this.

Though not yet officially released by CAT, snippets of the tech giant’s launch video have been leaking through dealers and trade journals, and they show the big machine powered by CAT’s newest 18.1 liter Tier 5 C18 diesel generator making 527 hp (~390 kW). That C18 reportedly sends electrons to the same electric drive system used in the company’s already successful 18-ton R2900 XE LHD.

In addition to a bigger generator and heftier payload, CAT says the upcoming R3200 XE LHD offers reduced cycle times versus the R2900 XE with 11% better speed on grade, plus reduced maintenance and repair costs thanks to design refinements for better durability, including redesigned axle. All told, that works out to 28% more tons per hour with 8% better fuel efficiency.

That efficiency is boosted by the same baked-in ADAS tech that’s made the smaller R2900 XE a favorite, and includes the latest version of CAT AutoDig and MineStar, ensuring that the machines are easy for experienced CAT operators to set up for remote, semi-autonomous, and even fully autonomous operation using Command for Underground.

According to recent reports, we’ll post an patch once CAT makes the full rundown of official specs public, which should be sooner rather than later. When that happens, we’ll see exactly how this big burrowing CAT stacks up against the competition from Sandvik, Epiroc, and Komatsu. In the meantime, let us know what you think of CAT’s newest electric drive machine in the comments.

The impact also seems to have spilled over into crypto, with the total market cap forming its third consecutive lower low at $2.08 trillion, a level last seen in early Q3.

In a recent development, naturally, this raises a question: Is crypto’s weakness simply a result of ANT-driven volatility? Interestingly, recent Glassnode data points to a possible link. As the chart below shows, Anthropic futures on crypto platforms recorded $9.5 billion in trading volume ahead of its Nasdaq debut. In comparison, SpaceX, the largest IPO on record, attracted $3.9 billion in pre-listing futures volume before its June debut.

In essence, ANT’s pre-IPO futures generated more than 2.4x SpaceX’s.

Recent findings suggest that this highlights how much larger speculative interest in ANT was compared to SpaceX, setting a upcoming record for pre-IPO trading activity on crypto platforms. However, the initial hype quickly turned into profit-taking, with ANT dropping 13% from its opening price. This shift in sentiment may have added to Bitcoin’s [BTC] selling pressure, especially as liquidation activity picked up alongside the broader market breakdown.

So, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

It looks like ANT’s futures activity on crypto platforms may have added to the selling pressure.

According to CoinGlass, over $700 million worth of positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly $600 million was long positions, indicating that leveraged bulls have been badly hit by the correction. However, can this flush-out in Futures markets lead to a rebalance?

According to recent reports, worth mentioning here is the ongoing liquidity drain. In the last 30 days, $11.5 billion has left the stablecoin supply. That outflow is greater than it was in the aftermath of the Terra collapse in 2022. While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

Why does this matter? Lower stablecoin supply means less available liquidity to support buying activity, which could keep pressure on Bitcoin and the broader market.

So, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.

Against this backdrop, a drop in the total crypto market cap below $2 trillion cannot be ruled out.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Polestar has now fully unveiled the Formula 2030 concept, a low four-door electric sports car that previews the design of the next-generation Polestar 2 coming in 2027 and the Polestar 7 compact SUV.
  • The concept sits just 1,350 mm (53 inches) tall, which is lower than the Polestar 5 grand tourer, and it brings physical buttons back into the Swedish brand’s interior.
