📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Polestar has now fully unveiled the Formula 2030 concept, a low four-door electric sports car that previews the design of the next-generation Polestar 2 coming in 2027 and the Polestar 7 compact SUV.

The concept sits just 1,350 mm (53 inches) tall, which is lower than the Polestar 5 grand tourer, and it brings physical buttons back into the Swedish brand’s interior.

Recent findings suggest that we reported in September that Polestar confirmed the Formula 2030 concept after showing it privately to investors and retailers in Gothenburg. Now we get the full set of pictures and the details.

It’s the first show car built under head of design Philipp Römers, who joined from Audi in 2024.

Polestar calls the Formula 2030 a “compact practical four-door sports car” that “sits within its own segment.” It’s 4,680 mm (184.3 inches) long and 2,021 mm (79.6 inches) wide, on a 2,780 mm (109.4-inch) wheelbase.

For context, that’s about 3 inches longer than today’s Polestar 2 and roughly 5 inches lower. It’s also a bit shorter than a Tesla Model 3 and sits 3.5 inches closer to the ground. Polestar notes the concept lands “somewhere between” the upcoming Polestar 2 and Polestar 7 in size.

It has been revealed that the proportions are classic sports car: long hood, short overhangs, the cabin pushed back over major rear haunches, and 22-inch center-lock wheels. There are gold Brembo calipers behind those wheels and Öhlins dampers on display in the trunk.

Up front, Polestar kept its “Dual Blade” headlights, now set into an aero wing over a shark nose and a deep splitter. The automaker notes this is the face of the next-generation Polestar 2 planned for 2027.

There’s a single vertical windshield wiper, like on a race car, and a LiDAR unit that hides under an aerodynamic shroud and only demonstrates itself when the car is driving autonomously.

In a recent development, the rear is where things change the most. Polestar dropped the full-width light bar, which is on just about every EV these days, for what it calls “Single Blade” rear lights. It states they are being introduced here “ahead of series production.”.

Römers described the concept as a “bold evolution” of the brand’s existing design:.

“It is a physical embodiment of how we apply Polestar’s core values of design, performance and sustainability to the next production cars.”.

The rear doors are hinged at the back and there’s no B-pillar, so the whole side opens up to four individual seats.

Sources indicate that the interior is built around the driver. A curved 20-inch display, which Polestar calls the “HyperDIM,” is mounted directly on the steering column, and a 12.2-inch center screen sits in the center tunnel.

But the bigger news is below that screen. Polestar added a panel of eight physical controls for the most-used functions, and owners could swap between types of controls, like rocker switches or rotary knobs, and program what each one does.

Polestar notes it is “committing to rebalance the mix of physical and digital.” Juan Pablo Bernal, the company’s head of interior design, put it plainly:.

Recent findings suggest that “As a performance brand, we see a renewed focus on the driver, and so we re-balance the digital and physical. We introduce physical buttons and controls.”.

That’s a substantial change for a brand whose recent cars run almost everything through the center touchscreen.

According to recent reports, the cabin also physically changes with the drive mode. There are three of them: Performance, Normal, and Autonomous. In Performance, the center screen drops flush into the console and the steering wheel and its display pull closer to the driver. In Autonomous, the wheel and the seat move away from each other.

The four seats use inflatable bolsters that shape themselves to each occupant, and the seat backs are made of a flax-based composite instead of virgin plastic. Google Gemini is built in, like in Polestar’s production cars.

According to recent reports, the cargo area is the strangest part of the car. The rear opens as a clamshell, and the trunk floor is transparent, with custom Polestar bags strapped down underneath it with gold straps.

Up front, the frunk holds two race helmets and a fire extinguisher, framed by a gold strut brace.

It has been revealed that now for what’s missing. Polestar didn’t release a single powertrain spec. No battery size, no range, no power output, and no price. This is a design study, and Polestar isn’t saying it will build it.

What it does say is that “various design attributes” from the concept will show up on the next Polestar 2 in 2027 and the Polestar 7 in 2028. Those are two of the four latest models Polestar looks to launch in three years, and the 7 is going to be built in Europe.

Industry observers note that europe is where this matters, since Polestar is shut out of the US under the federal connected-vehicle rule. The concept made its debut during the media drive of the Polestar 4 SUV.

Polestar always impresses me with its design, and this is no exception with this upcoming head of design.

Recent findings suggest that the proportions are sharp. Long hood, cabin pushed back, major haunches, and a roofline lower than the Polestar 5’s on a car with four doors and four real seats. If the next Polestar 2 keeps even half of this stance, it’s going to be the best-looking car in its segment.

In a recent development, I have loved Polestar from the day they introduced. Every car they design is a work of art and I love their commitment to transparency and sustainablitity. The 2023 Polestar 2 is still one of my favorite cars I've ever owned. I've driven the 3 and the 4 and both were fantastic. The fit and finish, ride and build quality, and NVH were all excellent. The upgraded 3 was probably going to be my next car in 2027 until they were forced to withdraw from the US. I think their future with the new 2 and 7 are bright and I'm still hoping (though I'm not holding my breath) that they will return to the US at some point. If the 5 was available here, I'd buy it today.

Sources indicate that I don’t know about the trunk of this thing. Polestar itself calls the rear “UFO-esque,” and between the wraparound glass, the clamshell and the see-through floor, it’s a lot. But everything else on this car is pretty sharp.

Sources indicate that polestar is putting physical controls back in its cars and saying so in plain words. The way they talk about it makes it sound like you can expect that of upcoming production vehicles.

Now the usual caveat. A concept car doesn’t fix a balance sheet. Polestar lost $842 million in the first half of this year on a negative gross margin. Design has never been Polestar’s problem. Building these cars and selling them at a profit is.

The two later maturities in the same Spectra overview had about $51,000 and $13,000, so holders seeking another fixed rate would have to trade in a much smaller pool.

The gap was visible in Spectra’s market overview on Nov. 19, which shows that its later pools mature on Dec. 31 and March 31, 2027. The first question for Spectra holders at maturity is which token the position can deliver on Flare.

It has been revealed that firelight takes FXRP, the representation of XRP on the Flare network, and complications stXRP shares in its vault. On Spectra, a buyer can purchase a principal token at a discount and redeem it at maturity.

This November series has its own market on Flare, which lists stXRP as the default input or output and FXRP as the underlying asset.

At maturity, Spectra holders can open their positions to see the available redemption token and estimated proceeds. Spectra’s redemption guide demonstrates the underlying payout is normally close to one unit per principal token, with a lower rate possible if the strategy suffers a loss.

Industry observers note that spectra’s contracts also support redemption in the interest-bearing token. In that case, the output also depends on the conversion rate. According to recent reports, both the swap and the rollover depend on what the market will fill for a given amount of stXRP. Meanwhile, Firelight’s unstaking process records the share value in FXRP when the holder requests a withdrawal and ends reward accrual at that point.

According to recent reports, as of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

In a recent development, TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG firm that builds on Bittensor.

Sources indicate that at Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert noted that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence.".

Industry observers note that on Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson noted.

The gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

In a recent development, the November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

According to recent reports, SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

According to recent reports, TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

Shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the early hours of the 20th of November saw Bitcoin [BTC] trading at $61,678 after a staggering 9.7% drop in the last 24 hours. Ethereum [ETH], following the crypto bloodbath, traded at $1,732 after experiencing a 3.7% slide in this time frame.

The crypto market’s current downfall is primarily due to persistent Spot ETF outflows and lingering fallout from last month’s Binance breach, which are making investors wary.

As the global cryptocurrency market cap fell 2.2% to $2.21 trillion in the last 24 hours at press time, the Crypto Fear & Greed Index slid to 12, indicating “extreme fear.”.

It has been revealed that after $306.5 million left Spot Bitcoin ETFs on the 18th of November, CoinGlass data showed that $582.3 million in outflows on the following day,  pushing this month’s outflows well past the $2.9 billion mark. Continued ETF bleeding signals that buyers continue to exit, leaving the market quite vulnerable to macro volatility.

Similarly, minutes from the October FOMC meeting, released on the 18th of November, showed that nearly all officials expect further rate hikes. Notably, Governor Christopher Waller even floated a half-point move for December.

With the Fed target at 3.75%–4.00%, digital assets will not have an easy battle.

It has been revealed that ever since investors have moved away from crypto and into AI, the former’s fall has been nearly constant. For the uninitiated, on the 18th of November, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, thus valuing the AI firm at roughly $1.5 trillion.

The news drew massive investor attention, pulling capital away from crypto markets as a result.

Regardless, the long-term sentiment of crypto investors has already been sullied due to the October 29 Binance hack that resulted in $6.3 billion in stolen funds.

The crypto bloodbath will likely continue unless ETF flows stabilize or the Fed signals a pause. With the December 9 FOMC meeting as the only upcoming checkpoint, 60,000 is the next level for traders to watch. Losing it can tip Bitcoin deeper into the mid-50,000s.

Industry observers note that an Abu Dhabi court has ordered Circle and 17 other companies to keep tokens linked to Binance’s Oct. 29 theft frozen while the exchange tries to recover them.

In a recent development, binance disclosed the order on Nov. 18 and stated some issuers, exchanges and other partners ask for a court order before they will release or transfer assets they have frozen.

The exchange said the order from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts helps open that route, describing ongoing efforts to trace the stolen funds and giving no details of any transfer under the order.

The named firms include Circle, which complications USDC, and World Liberty Financial, the manufacturer behind USD1.

Reports noted that the firms must maintain the freezes pending further proceedings and cannot lend, swap, or mix the affected tokens with other assets.

The court did not accuse the firms of wrongdoing, and Dec. 1 is scheduled to consider whether to keep the injunction in place and on what terms.

Sources indicate that the injunction covers specific assets Binance claimed are tied to the theft, and said it is still tracing the stolen crypto and taking legal steps to reclaim it. A transfer for firms seeking a court order depends on whether they have authority to release the specific balances they have frozen.

In a recent development, tether falls outside the order covering the 18 firms, and the company remarked on Nov. 2 it had frozen more than $1.5 billion tied to the theft.

A spokesperson stated Tether would work directly with Binance to reissue the tokens, in consultation with the relevant authorities.

It has been revealed that the Abu Dhabi order directs 18 firms to maintain freezes. Tether states it will work separately with Binance on reissuing USDT.

Binance is still seeking the return of assets held under the court order.

The tracks show procedural steps. The Dec. 1 hearing and Tether’s plan leave the timing of any return open.

Industry observers note that the Abu Dhabi order follows earlier US court action. On Nov. 12, the US Justice Department mentioned it had obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in stolen crypto. That was part of more than $2.7 billion that US authorities and private firms had helped freeze.

In its Nov. 3 incident report, Binance estimated that about $6.3 billion in digital assets were affected and about $2.85 billion was frozen or intercepted, subject to reconciliation and market prices.

According to recent reports, the separate disclosures do not establish how much the figures overlap or how much Binance can ultimately recover. Binance says it absorbed the financial impact on customers while continuing to pursue the stolen assets.

Latest Update: Lucid claims service wait times fell 20% after 40% jump in service staff

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lucid (LCID) notes service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.
  • Industry observers note that the automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans.
  • Industry observers note that lucid announced the numbers today, a day after its Q3 2026 earnings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lucid (LCID) notes service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.

Industry observers note that the automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans. It’s a clear sign that service had become a problem for Lucid owners.

Industry observers note that lucid announced the numbers today, a day after its Q3 2026 earnings. Both comparisons are against the second quarter, not a year ago.

The hiring isn’t done either. After a 40%-plus increase in technicians, advisors, and concierges in Q3, Lucid wants that figure at 50% by the end of 2026 and 60% by Q1 2027. Mobile Service capacity in North America grew 15%, with a 40% target for year-end.

That’s a significant hiring push for a manufacturer that laid off 18% of its workforce in June, its second cut in four months after a 12% reduction in February. Roughly 1,500 people left across those two rounds.

And owners noticed. On the LucidOwners forum, one Air Touring owner posted in early October that Lucid told them in writing to expect “a service time of about 7 weeks” at its Beverly Hills Service Center. Other threads blamed service-department layoffs for slow repairs and recall work.

Billy Hayes, Lucid’s Chief Customer Officer, remarked the organization is “adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support.”.

Here’s what’s opening, according to Lucid:.

Lucid is also letting a growing number of its Certified Collision shops handle recall campaign work, which should take some pressure off its own Service Centers.

Outside the US, the expansion leans on partners. Munsterhuis Autobedrijven is Lucid’s first retail partner in the Netherlands (Hengelo), Cloppenburg Automobil SE opens a Duisburg retail and service site in January 2027, Autohaus Possögel starts authorized service in Naumburg, Germany, in December, and Emil Frey France will support Lucid’s launch in France. In Saudi Arabia, Lucid opened its first organization-owned Body & Paint Repair Center in Riyadh, with more service sites in Riyadh and Dammam coming in the first half of 2027.

Lucid doesn’t say what the average wait time actually is.

A 20% drop from seven weeks is still more than five weeks. A 20% drop from one week is a non-glitch. Without a baseline, owners can’t tell which one they’re getting.

Sources indicate that it’s also hard to separate better service from fewer cars coming in. Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while it worked through inventory. Its fleet keeps growing, but slowly.

For context, Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3, five times Lucid’s volume, and it’s been leaning hard on mobile service too. Lucid is a much smaller operation trying to cover the US, Europe, and the Middle East with a thin network.

This is the right move, and it’s overdue.

Recent findings suggest that lucid has been one of the few EV startups with genuinely class-leading hardware. The Air’s efficiency is still unmatched and the Gravity is a great vehicle on paper, even if we found its software wasn’t ready. But when you’re asking someone to spend $80,000 or more on a car from a brand with an uncertain future, the ownership experience is half the sale. A seven-week wait for a repair kills that sale, and the referrals that come after it.

Sources indicate that so growing service staff by 40% in a quarter is a massive deal. It also tells you how thin those teams had gotten after two rounds of layoffs. Lucid cut too deep in the wrong place, and it’s now hiring to fix it.

The problem is the timing and the money. Lucid burned $1.04 billion in free cash flow in Q3 and only stays funded into late 2027 because the PIF just added another $1.75 billion. Meanwhile, the Midsize “Cosmos” that’s supposed to bring real volume doesn’t start production until the second half of 2027. Service is exactly where Lucid should spend between now and then, because the buyers it has today are the ones who’ll decide whether anybody trusts the brand with a cheaper EV.

Theaster Gates is Changing the Future of American Fine China

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (956 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it all started when Theaster Gates wanted to throw a dinner party.
  • Recent findings suggest that “My friends were like, ‘Oh, you should work with Pickard,’ ” Gates recalls, referring to the last remaining producer of porcelain tableware in the US, founded in 1893 and headquartered since 1930 in Antioch, Illinois.
  • Recent findings suggest that “I came to the warehouse and realized that the organization had had better days,” Gates claims.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it all started when Theaster Gates wanted to throw a dinner party. The Chicago-based artist, whose practice blends ceramics, painting, performance, and urban renewal, imagined inviting 200 guests on each of five nights. Central to the project, he envisioned creating all the tableware himself.

Recent findings suggest that “My friends were like, ‘Oh, you should work with Pickard,’ ” Gates recalls, referring to the last remaining producer of porcelain tableware in the US, founded in 1893 and headquartered since 1930 in Antioch, Illinois. When he told Pickard he would need some 10,000 items, the firm admitted such an order would be daunting but invited him to visit.

Recent findings suggest that “I came to the warehouse and realized that the organization had had better days,” Gates claims. “I’m wanting to say this with a lot of dignity, but as we moved between tarps and equipment, it became clear that the company was just doing what it could to stay alive.”.

China dishware fills two rolling racks at the Pickard factory in Illinois, which was recently purchased by Theaster Gates.

Gates at the Pickard facility with molds for dishware.

Recent findings suggest that pickard’s august history of commissions includes White House services for first ladies Laura Bush and Michelle Obama, as well as the official State Department dinnerware used in US embassies around the world. Once an essential element of bridal registries, fine china has waned in popularity, however, along with the tradition of formal entertaining at home. After CEO Andy Pickard Morgan, a member of the fourth generation of the family to run the business, acknowledged that he was ready to call it a day, one thing led to another, and Gates indicates, “I am now the owner of Pickard China.”.

His acquisition might seem out of character. Gates has forged a formidable reputation for himself and his Rebuild Foundation by buying rundown buildings in Chicago’s historically Black South Side, then converting them into thriving arts and education hubs. An abandoned residence is now the Black Cinema House; a century-old savings and loan is now the Stony Island Arts Bank, which mounts exhibitions and safeguards historical collections. Pickard, meanwhile, is located in a quiet, predominantly white village on the Wisconsin border, some 67 miles from his studio on Chicago’s South Side.

A Pickard artisan finishing a plate.

Gates, funnel in hand, surrounded by artifacts of the Pickard process.

Pickard pieces line plywood racks.

Industry observers note that but Gates does not see a contradiction. For starters, he indicates, his interest in craft transcends racial or ethnic origins; one formative experience was studying with master potters in Japan. Gates notes that while many of his collections relate to Black culture, he also took on the late scholar Robert Bird’s library of films by the Russian director Andrei Tarkovsky and the classical music archive of the LaSalle Quartet, whose core members were Jewish. “I have those because they are rich, and someone passed, and those things needed a latest life,” he explains. “The problem of the archive is not one of Black or white; it’s one of stewardship and imagination.” He has even shown an affinity for luxury goods, having made ceramic vessels for Prada Home in Milan this past April.

Pickard also presents the kind of big, multifaceted problem Gates, who holds a master’s degree in urban planning, indicates “makes me feel alive as an artist,” in this case encompassing craftsmanship and legacy, as well as the value of labor and community. His aims are still developing but include upgrading the facilities, rethinking the product line, and beefing up the staff, which now stands at 14 full-time employees, down from dozens at the organization’s height. Preserving their know-how for posterity is a priority. “I want this really capable team to train a fresh generation of descalers and liners and glazers,” he says. Also definite: The company will continue operating in the commercial sphere, and he will use its massive kilns to fire his own large sculptures, something he’s wanted to do for a decade. “I’m thinking about manufacturing ceramics as an extension of my practice,” he notes.

A Pickard artisan filling molds.

The Pickard logo emblazoned on a wall.

In a recent development, gates has worked with a variety of materials over the years, including tar paper—a nod to his roofer father—and salvaged fire hoses, which reference Civil Rights Era marchers who were blasted with water by police. Ceramics, though, were the focus of his formal studies and remain at the heart of his practice. “When I was training, I touched porcelain, but I was always a rough stoneware guy,” he says. “The more grog and sand and feldspar, the better.”.

Today Gates considers porcelain “an amazing craft” and expects the workshop to become “a playground for artistic promise,” where he, together with staff and visiting artists alike, can “dream about a raw material that could be anything.”.

Setting the table with bone china may no longer be the signifier of position and civility it once was, but Gates believes there’s still room for appreciation, as both an instrument of ritual and a family heirloom. “Legacy objects play a huge role in how we remember our grandparents, our parents, and our past,” he claims.

Industry observers note that and Gates’s own party is very much still on the table, so to speak. “Porcelain things are beautiful objects, but I’m drawn as much to the use of the thing as I am to the thing,” he notes. “The idea that I could make large works of art with porcelain is exciting, but I’m also excited to be able to host a thousand-person dinner and make all the wares for it.”.

Significant long liquidations were seen for Zcash, accelerating its price decline as leveraged positions unwind, particularly with traders being heavily concentrated on the same side of the market.

At the time of writing, ZEC was down 14.53% in the last 24 hours, recording the heaviest losses in the top 20, while NEAR Protocol was down 13.03% in the same timeframe.

Sources indicate that zcash is currently testing support at the 200-day MA ($809); a further drop would target $775 and then $700. A short-term price recovery for Zcash would see it aim for a return to four figures, eyeing the 50-day MA at $1,164.

Industry observers note that zcash is entering its third day of a drop that began on November 18, even as the broader crypto market slid as the tech-stock selloff spread. The rapid unwind suggests a leverage shakeout amid volatility following Anthropic’s IPO.

Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, under the ticker symbol ANT, raising about $81.3 billion in the public offering (and $107.3 billion combined with a $26 billion private placement).

In a recent development, over the last 24 hours, volume across crypto futures rose 29.31% to $250 billion, while open interest (OI) fell 3.07% to $109.29 billion, according to CoinGlass data. That combination suggests traders are unwinding positions, with net capital exiting the futures market.

Liquidations across the crypto market increased by 88.66% to $773.76 million, and longs accounted for 87.2% of the total, meaning leveraged bets on higher prices were forced shut as prices fell.

Ranking was based on time-weighted holdings, which encouraged accumulation and retention through the window.

More than 5,000 eligible holders reportedly did not register. The leaderboard’s combined value represented only a small fraction of TRUMP’s roughly $268 million market capitalization.

Sources indicate that TRUMP was trading around $0.95 in the latest reporting, down roughly 46% over the prior month after setting a record low near $0.896 on November 14. The token remains well below its peak, with one account describing it as down almost 99% from its high.

Large holders added to positions during the dip. Nansen data demonstrated the top 100 wallets increased their combined holdings by 1.27% over 30 days, while a separate whale cohort expanded holdings by 26.63%. Exchange balances fell slightly over the same period.

Holding incentives are temporary.

Top-ranked winners risk losing VIP benefits if balances drop below specified levels before the event, and lower-ranked winners can forfeit their seat by selling more than half their qualifying balance. Those restrictions expire once the dinner is over.

Ahead of the 2025 dinner, 92 of 220 invited holders reportedly sold their entire positions before the event.

A Super Bowl-themed leaderboard planned for February 2027 may give some buyers a reason to stay involved, but it does not remove the immediate question of whether winners will take liquidity afterward.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility.
  • According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is presently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.
  • According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is presently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further highlights that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is important to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

Recent findings suggest that at the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data shows that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

#6185. Unit1 FARO and NEON review: I just found my latest favorite e-bike helmets

Unit1 FARO and NEON review: I just found my latest favorite e-bike helmets

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I test a lot of electric bikes, which means I also spend a lot of time wearing bicycle helmets.
  • I’ve been using both the UNIT 1 FARO and the fresh NEON, and despite taking fairly different approaches, they’ve both become regular go-to helmets for me.
  • The FARO is the more futuristic-looking of the two, and it’s also the one that really leans into the “smart helmet” concept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I test a lot of electric bikes, which means I also spend a lot of time wearing bicycle helmets. And while most helmets tend to fall into the decidedly unexciting category of “necessary safety equipment,” UNIT 1 has managed to make a couple that I actually get excited about wearing.

I’ve been using both the UNIT 1 FARO and the fresh NEON, and despite taking fairly different approaches, they’ve both become regular go-to helmets for me.

The FARO is the more futuristic-looking of the two, and it’s also the one that really leans into the “smart helmet” concept.

The helmet includes MIPS protection to reduce rotational impact during a collision, as well as integrated lighting on both the front and rear, including a large customizable rear lighting area made up of dozens of LEDs.

That large rear LED array is a feature I particularly appreciate since visibility is such a major part of cycling safety.

According to recent reports, A helmet obviously can’t force drivers to pay attention, but I’d rather give them as many opportunities as possible to see me. The hidden light area below the obvious LED light bar adds a lot of extra visibility.

You can see just how vivid it is in the GIF below, though in real life it looks even better!

The FARO’s lighting system works with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote, which adds turn signals controlled right from the bars.

The system can also provide automatic brake-light functionality, giving you another way to communicate with traffic around you.

Industry observers note that I’ll admit that turn signals on bicycles can sometimes feel a bit gimmicky, especially when they’re so close together that drivers can’t really tell which direction is flashing. But putting them high up on the helmet makes them considerably more visible, and the little wireless handlebar remote makes operating them incredibly easy.

Recent findings suggest that the rechargeable lighting is also convenient. I’ve topped up the helmet from a power bank while out and about, meaning you don’t necessarily need to find a wall outlet if you realize your helmet is running low. The rear LED light bar also turns green and illuminates along the length of the bar to let you know what percentage of charge the battery has reached. The only way it could be clearer would be with a screen, but we’re still talking about a helmet here, not a phone.

There are other smart features packed in too, including crash detection and app-based customization.

The tradeoff is weight. At around 640 grams for a medium, the FARO is noticeably heavier than a conventional bicycle helmet. It doesn’t bother me much once I’m riding, and I’ve found the helmet comfortable, but you definitely know there’s more helmet up there. Each time I pick it up, I’m reminded that it’s not just the basic little foam shell that I’ve been wearing for the last few years.

Then there’s the price. At around $230 (or $195 during the current Black Friday sale period), this isn’t a cheap helmet. You’re paying for all of that technology, lighting, and design.

As much as I like the FARO, I’ve also become a substantial fan of the UNIT 1 NEON.

At roughly 430 grams in a medium, it’s significantly lighter than the FARO, and that difference is immediately noticeable. It’s also a bit cheaper at around $210 (or $178 during the Black Friday sale period) while still packing several of the smart features that make UNIT 1’s helmets interesting.

You still get MIPS rotational protection, crash detection, integrated rear lighting, app connectivity, and compatibility with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote for turn signals and brake-light functionality.

Sources indicate that I do wish the NEON had a front light like the FARO. That’s probably the biggest feature I miss when switching between the two. But the NEON makes up for it with one of my favorite features on either helmet: its magnetic face shield.

Industry observers note that the shield is ridiculously easy to attach and remove. You don’t even need to carefully line it up. I just need to get it somewhere near the mounting points with one hand and the powerful magnets basically grab it out of the air and snap it into position.

That means I can easily add or remove it one-handed, even while riding.

The photochromic shield is clear enough for night riding but darkens when exposed to bright sunlight, giving you sun protection without requiring separate daytime and nighttime shields. I’ve found that incredibly convenient, especially on rides that transition from daylight into evening. I hate that I can’t wear my sunglasses for eye protection at night, and a lens like this solves that concern.

Recent findings suggest that the NEON also gets something particularly crucial for faster e-bike riders: NTA 8776 certification. That’s the Dutch standard designed specifically around higher-speed e-bike uses at up to 45 km/h (28 mph). For the Class 3 e-bikes that have become increasingly common in the US, that’s a major distinction compared to helmets rated for crashes at slower speeds.

That’s actually difficult, because I regularly use both.

Recent findings suggest that the FARO is the one I’d choose if maximum visibility and technology were my priorities. I love having LEDs both front and rear, the MIPS protection, and the handlebar-controlled turn signals. It’s comfortable, looks great, and has become one of my favorite urban riding helmets.

But the NEON may be the easier helmet to recommend to most e-bike riders.

It’s lighter, a little cheaper, still gives you a rear light and smart safety features, has that excellent magnetic photochromic face shield, and importantly carries NTA 8776 certification for faster e-bike riding.

Recent findings suggest that neither helmet is inexpensive, and the FARO in particular asks you to accept some extra weight in exchange for all that technology. But I’m used to wearing much heavier motorcycle helmets and ways.

Plus, it’s important to note that these aren’t helmets I tested for a few rides and then tossed onto a shelf. Both have stayed in my regular rotation, and I find myself reaching for them frequently when I head out on an e-bike. The fact that I not only enjoyed them during my testing but actually replaced my old helmets with them should speak for itself.

For someone who rides as much as I do, that’s probably the strongest endorsement I can give them.

Between solid helmets like these and safe riding clothing, it’s good to feel protected!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinbase has opened a portion of Deribit’s options market to eligible customers outside the US, with contracts in Coinbase Advanced settling in USDC and falling into a product category that accounted for about 2% of Deribit’s October options turnover.

In a recent development, in two matched calls sampled on Nov. 19, USDC contracts had narrower spreads, while coin-settled contracts offered buyers more size at the best price.

On the same day, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong revealed on X that crypto options were live for non-US customers.

It has been revealed that the Coinbase Advanced options guide names Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Hyperliquid, and XRP. All six use linear contracts, where traders pay the premium in USDC and in-the-money positions ultimately settle in the same stablecoin.

Coinbase directs customers to check eligibility in the app and complete derivatives onboarding where the service is offered. Coinbase had described a phased rollout in its earlier integration guidance.

The options rollout follows Coinbase’s Oct. 1 migration of its International Exchange (ICE) business to Deribit. The latest change lets eligible Coinbase Advanced people trade options from their existing Coinbase account, including through the app, on the infrastructure that already powers their international perpetuals.

It has been revealed that deribit’s October turnover report puts USDC options at $1.35 billion of $68.6 billion in total reported options turnover, or 1.97%. The BTC- and ETH-settled categories accounted for about $67.25 billion combined.

Deribit reports the inverse categories in dollar terms even though the contracts settle in their underlying coins.

Sources indicate that october turnover in billions of U.S. dollars was 58.71 for BTC-settled options, 8.53 for ETH-settled options and 1.35 for USDC-settled options across assets.

Source: Monthly Statistics · · Linear contracts · · Inverse contracts.

In a recent development, the USDC category covers multiple assets, so 1.97% describes activity for the venue’s full linear category before the announcement. The price and size a customer can trade depend on the orders available for the individual strike and expiration.

Recent findings suggest that cryptoSlate sampled two Nov. 27 calls on Deribit between 20:11:50 and 20:12:36 UTC on Nov. 19, matching underlying asset, strike and expiration across settlement currencies. In both cases, the USDC book had the narrower quoted gap between the highest bid and lowest ask. The coin-settled book highlighted more size at the price a buyer could take.

For the $64,000 Bitcoin call, the USDC book revealed a 25 USDC spread and 10 BTC of underlying exposure offered at the best ask. The BTC-settled book showed a spread equivalent to $31.03 and 25.9 BTC available at its best ask.

In a recent development, for the $1,800 Ethereum call, the USDC book showed a 0.80 USDC spread and 150 ETH at the best ask. Its ETH-settled counterpart showed a spread equivalent to $0.88 and 1,642 ETH offered at its best ask.

Industry observers note that the size advantage flipped for sellers trading at the best bid. At that price, buyers were seeking 20.01 BTC and 116.1 ETH of exposure in the USDC books, compared with 12.8 BTC and 29 ETH in the coin-settled books.

In two matched Deribit calls, the USDC books had more size at the best bid and the coin-settled books had more at the best ask.

In these two calls, which book indicated more size depended on whether the trader wanted to buy or sell.

CryptoSlate converted coin-denominated premiums using the index price in each Deribit order-book response and compared USDC with dollars at approximate parity.

It has been revealed that coinbase mentioned on Nov. 4 that global options and perpetuals were live on Prime for eligible institutions in the US and other supported markets. Its Prime product list includes USDC-settled linear options and inverse options priced and settled in BTC or ETH, both allowing long and short positions.

Institutions must qualify as Eligible Contract Participants, complete the application and portfolio activation, and sign the clearing and Deribit agreements. Orders route through Coinbase Financial Markets and a foreign broker’s risk controls to Deribit’s matching engine.

The Prime venue terms list USDC, BTC, and ETH as collateral, with standard or portfolio margin by portfolio and settlement currency. Daily settlement takes place at 08:00 UTC, and the Global Derivatives portfolio’s margin is kept separate from spot and US derivatives.

#6182. 5 New Retail Design Rules, According to Experts

📖 Baca

5 New Retail Design Rules, According to Experts

📅 06 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that when nearly anything can be bought with a few taps on a screen, brick-and-mortar stores have to work harder—and smarter—to earn a visit.
  • The first goal for any latest retail space is obvious: Make people want to be there.
  • Fashion designer Danielle Frankel Hirsch just opened a 12,000-square-foot studio in Tribeca, collaborating with Studio Partners Architecture and AD PRO Directory designer Augusta Hoffman to create a gasp-worthy dress boutique worthy of any bride's fantasies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when nearly anything can be bought with a few taps on a screen, brick-and-mortar stores have to work harder—and smarter—to earn a visit. What e-commerce can't replicate, even with the cleverest algorithms, is the thrill of stepping into a beautifully conceived space—and discovering something you didn't know you wanted. From side-by-side jewel-box fashion boutiques in Paris to a palatial bridal studio set in a 19th-century building in downtown New York, AD PRO highlights the massive ideas shaping today’s most engaging retail environments.

The first goal for any latest retail space is obvious: Make people want to be there.

Fashion designer Danielle Frankel Hirsch just opened a 12,000-square-foot studio in Tribeca, collaborating with Studio Partners Architecture and AD PRO Directory designer Augusta Hoffman to create a gasp-worthy dress boutique worthy of any bride's fantasies. Located in a 19th century edifice originally built to house the New York Mercantile Exchange, the shop, indicates Frankel Hirsch, is designed as a transportive experience. After guests enter the space through its unassuming Tribeca storefront entrance, they ascend a grand carpeted staircase to a large gallery boasting over 30-foot floor-to-ceiling windows. Hoffman worked with artist Miriam Ellner to create églomisé paneling surrounding the staircase, and outfitted the spaces to the height of elegance, with Fortuny fabrics, furniture sourced from Paris, and handpainted ceiling murals.

The 30-foot ceilings at Newly introduced York City's Danielle Frankel guarantee a wedding dress shopping experience that's hard to equal.

Recent findings suggest that in Paris, Rubirosa's two petite boutiques, designed by Louis Charles Aka, deliver a similar sense of occasion on a much smaller scale. The original 500-square-foot shop, which opened in June 2025, was joined this past August by a second location just next door. Rather than simply duplicate the first boutique's nostalgic formality, Aka has given its latest neighbor a distinct personality. The lacquered shelving remains, displaying cashmere sweaters, crisp poplin shirts, and soft leather slippers in a rainbow of colors. But where the original featured tall bookcases, the new shop has floor-to-ceiling arches whose cubbies become bands of color when filled with garments of cashmere, cotton, and silk.

In the original boutique, the defining gesture was a dense, velvety red wall-to-wall carpet from La Maison Bineau. “I spent everything on the red carpet,” Aka declares. “People criticized, ‘You will have to change it in three months.’ I noted, ‘We don’t care. We want people to feel special.’” In the second shop, the color drama comes courtesy of vivid Yves Klein blue—a knowing wink to the fashion set. Voluminous white balloon drapery heightens the theatricality, suggesting a salon for elegant grand dames even as the boutique attracts a younger crowd of influencers and trendsetters.

Lacquered walls hung with portraits of Pope John Paul II and Mobutu Sese Seko at Rubirosa’s.

The exterior of Rubirosa’s on Rue de Grenelle in Paris.

AD100 designer Brigette Romanek took a more subtle approach to creating desire at Catherine Bloom for Nordstrom, an appointment-only shop in Los Angeles where Bloom, the department store’s Director of Luxury Styling, works with private clients. “I want to make people feel something,” claims Romanek. “A store should be a destination you look forward to.” Her use of paneled walls in camel, khaki, and rose suede, plus her signature mix of elements both edgy (the angular leather sofa) and delicate (the plasterwork ceiling) creates what she calls “a protected feeling” that makes the space feel worth seeking out.

Suede-paneled walls and ornate plasterwork at Catherine Bloom for Nordstrom.

A punchy red-orange “wallop” moment at Big Night’s West Village outpost.

Industry observers note that where Romanek’s space whispers intimacy, Katherine Lewin’s Massive Night shouts joy. The New York City shop Big Night, which sells brightly hued kitchen and entertaining goods, trades old-world refinement for modern exuberance. “People tell me they get a shot of serotonin walking into the store,” she states. Her brand’s signature color of punchy red-orange provides what she calls a “wallop”—an immediate sensory experience that registers before customers even process what they’re looking at. Handmade tiles from Smink Studio, screen-printed with bold geometric patterns, are mixed in unexpected color combinations throughout the West Village store.

FoundRae’s Aspen boutique, complete with velvety chairs, books, and intriguing display cases lined with handwritten letters, old photos, and found objects.

Once you’ve lured customers in, the next challenge is keeping them there. “If someone is waiting for their partner to try on 50 things, they need to be comfortable,” indicates Romanek, who installed upholstered chairs from her collection for Crate & Barrel inside individual dressing rooms. Meanwhile, curtains at the store stay closed at all times, enhancing the protected atmosphere that encourages clients to relax and take their time.

In a recent development, beth Hutchens, founder of fine jewelry line FoundRae, has turned lingering into an art form. The average customer stay at her fine jewelry boutiques—which include locations in Latest York, Miami, Los Angeles, Dallas, Palm Beach, and Aspen—is an hour and a half. It makes sense when you consider the cozy reading nooks well stocked with books and a rotating menu of complimentary snacks and wine.

The maze-like layout of Big Night’s West Village.

In the age of algorithmic shopping recommendations, physical retail can offer something genuinely different: the pleasure of stumbling upon the unexpected. When Lewin found Significant Night’s West Village location, for instance, it was a warren of small spaces and hidden corners that defied traditional notions of retail design. Rather than optimizing for efficient shopping (and increasing her renovation costs), she embraced the pre-existing layout and discovered that it primed shoppers’ sense of exploration and surprise. “The store feels like a house party with different things happening in different corners,” Lewin explains.

At Fishs Eddy's Brooklyn location, deliberately cluttered displays add to the sense of discovery.

At Fishs Eddy, the beloved New York City housewares shop founded in 1986, the thrill of the hunt has always been part of the appeal. Now, four decades after opening its original Manhattan location, the retailer has expanded with two new outposts, at Chelsea Market and in Brooklyn's Dumbo neighborhood. The latter, an ambitious 3,800-square-foot space, deliberately preserves the cheerfully cluttered, homespun aesthetic that has become the brand's calling card. Rather than give the larger store a slick makeover, founder Julie Gaines embraced the same informal, decidedly human approach to retail design: Vintage-style dishes, deadstock dinnerware, and offbeat glassware are piled high on reclaimed-wood displays and mismatched vintage furniture, evoking the warehouses where the original merchandise was discovered. Gaines describes her merchandising philosophy as “very direct: the way we found it in the warehouse.” But that seemingly improvised look takes effort. “We spend a lot of time looking like we don’t spend time,” she admits. An old-fashioned soda fountain serving egg creams and inexpensive drip coffee adds to the new store's convivial atmosphere.

FoundRae takes discovery to remarkable lengths. Hutchens installed fully realized miniature vignettes behind unmarked cupboard doors—doll-size rooms that include recreations of her own home and FoundRae boutiques, complete with furniture and art. Display cases feature what Hutchens calls a “menagerie of the ephemeral”—handwritten letters, old photos, and evocative found items loosely pinned behind the jewelry. Then there are the “Discovery Drawers”—wood-fronted, glass-topped compartments that hold one-of-a-kind pieces unique to each location (never photographed or featured online).

Sources indicate that at Sézane’s new 2,800-square-foot boutique on New York’s Upper East Side, designer Pierre Lacroix has created a similar element of surprise through a dramatic shift in mood. Dubbed L’Appartement on Madison Avenue, the space evokes a Parisian home crossed with an art gallery, with books, artwork by William Klein, and vintage furniture. Most of the boutique feels light and airy, with creamy walls, cerused oak parquet floors, and parchment light fixtures. But tucked off to one side is a small shoe salon, drenched in dark chocolate tones and moodily lit. The intimate, after hours lounge-like space offers an unexpected counterpoint to the rest of the shop.

Sézane’s newest shop, aka L’Appartement on Madison Avenue, designed by Pierre Lacroix.

The shoe salon at Sézane’s L’Appartement offers an unexpected change of atmosphere.

Even in Rubirosa’s tiny space, Aka has created moments of discovery. He’s filled the walls with oil portraits of Luciano Pavarotti, Pope John Paul II, and various international dictators—a quirky mix of imagery that gives the space a distinctive personality. Visual layers invite clients to continuously notice new details, rewarding repeat visits.

Recent findings suggest that wes Anderson calling! A particularly Instagrammable corner of Rubirosa’s.

Sources indicate that aka admits that Rubirosa’s Instagram-friendly storefront serves as what he calls “a lure”—beautiful enough that people stop to photograph it even if they don’t come inside. “Some people come just to take pictures in front,” he claims. The combination of the crimson carpet, dark lacquered millwork, and those quirky framed portraits creates an irresistibly photogenic and TikTok-friendly environment. Romanek’s thoughtful color palette and material mix at the Nordstrom boutique creates a similarly camera-ready backdrop. The social media effect, says Romanek, is simply a natural byproduct of creating a distinctive space. “When a space feels different, conversations about it happen,” she explains. “And that’s what we like. We like people talking about the experience.”.

At the Danielle Frankel bridal studio, the sheer spectacle reaches another level entirely. From the soaring ceilings to the grand staircase with its shimmering églomisé panels, the interiors offer no shortage of photo opportunities. But for a boutique devoted to dressing brides for what is, ideally, a once-in-a-lifetime occasion, perhaps a little over-the-top grandeur is exactly the point.

Sources indicate that hoffman worked with the artist Miriam Ellner to create églomisé paneling surrounding the staircase. “The eglomise is one of my favorite things,” says Danielle Frankel designer Frankel Hirsch. The result is staircase that not creates a heightened emotional atmosphere for in-store shoppers but also provides a dramatic backdrop for photography.

Sources indicate that hutchens believes retail design isn’t inextricably tied to scalability. “Ask yourself, if every store was your only store, what would you do and how would you invest in it and change it?” she says. “You evolve faster when you think that way.”.

While all seven FoundRae stores share some design DNA—Hutchens embeds her signature mythological symbols in floors, ceilings, and furniture throughout—each reflects its location. The Aspen boutique is swathed in green, alluding to the town’s namesake aspen trees, with a large marquetry sunburst as its centerpiece. The Palm Beach shop features gilded verre églomisé, while in Miami, a vintage Steinway grand piano with hand-applied gold symbols anchors the room. As a result, the stores feel both part of a cohesive brand while rooted in their specific communities.

Big Night’s location in Brooklyn’s Greenpoint.

Big Night’s Upper East Side outpost.

Even Lewin’s three Substantial Night locations—Brooklyn, West Village, and the Upper East Side, which she calls “sisters, not twins”—each have distinct personalities while maintaining the brand’s joyful, color-saturated identity. Lewin likens the Upper East Side shop to a Classic Six apartment and notes that the fresh millwork was designed to reflect an upscale, elevated home. Her cash desk placement in the West Village location, situated in the center of the largest room rather than tucked away, came from understanding that specific space and how her team could best interact with customers there.

It has been revealed that the thread connecting these diverse approaches is a fundamental understanding that physical retail can no longer compete with e-commerce on convenience or selection. But the best retail spaces offer atmosphere, discovery, community, and the experience of being somewhere that feels genuinely special. As Aka puts it, “Like a good movie, when it ends...if you don’t have the feeling you want to see it again, it was not that good.”.

Recent findings suggest that the back room of Rubirosa’s is painted in a pale baby blue, “like a boy’s little bedroom,” says Aka. “So when you take out your credit card, it doesn’t bother you. It’s like you’re on a pillow.”.

The latest Bitcoin price action adds further to concerns surrounding the future of the flagship cryptocurrency.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ethereum developers are leaning toward retaining Glamsterdam's gas rules despite 200 findings that could disrupt existing smart contracts.
  • 19 core developers meeting, participants expressed broad support for proceeding with the current specifications rather than introducing changes that could push the network upgrade into April or May 2027.
  • Developers tentatively targeted the week of Dec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethereum developers are leaning toward retaining Glamsterdam's gas rules despite 200 findings that could disrupt existing smart contracts.

During a Nov. 19 core developers meeting, participants expressed broad support for proceeding with the current specifications rather than introducing changes that could push the network upgrade into April or May 2027.

Developers tentatively targeted the week of Dec. 14 for testing on Ethereum's Hoodi network, potentially allowing a mainnet activation as early as mid-January. However, the schedule remains unconfirmed as teams address compatibility problems affecting existing applications.

Glamsterdam is designed to significantly expand Ethereum's capacity, potentially increasing its block gas limit from 60 million to 200 million, a more than threefold increase.

According to Ethereum research firm Ethlabs, the expansion would give applications more room to operate directly on Ethereum's main network while reducing congestion and transaction fees during periods of heavy demand.

However, achieving that capacity requires changing how Ethereum charges for certain computing operations and data storage.

Two proposals, EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, introduce newly introduced gas pricing and accounting rules that could invalidate assumptions built into existing smart contracts.

A ChainSecurity assessment identified 200 compatibility findings across its investigations and work coordinated by the Ethereum Foundation.

Industry observers note that of these, three were classified as high severity, 30 as medium and 167 as low. None was rated critical.

The assessment identified potential disruptions affecting bridges, exchanges, wallets, staking platforms, governance systems, and other infrastructure supporting Ethereum applications.

Industry observers note that most findings can be addressed through configuration changes, but 24 require smart contract upgrades or migrations. Potential consequences include interrupted operations, locked funds, and errors in reward accounting.

The problem stems partly from applications that rely on fixed gas allowances to perform specific operations. Under Glamsterdam's proposed rules, those allowances may no longer be sufficient to complete the same work.

Industry observers note that recent Juicebox V6 simulations demonstrated the consequences. Some transactions were recorded as successful even though internal payments failed or were skipped under the tested rules.

Ethlabs acknowledged that changing gas prices is necessary to support Ethereum's expansion but distinguished those changes from accounting modifications that introduced unexpected behavior.

The research firm argued that protocol developers must convince application developers of the upgrade's safety.

Despite the findings, Ethereum developers remain divided over whether modifying Glamsterdam's specifications would meaningfully improve compatibility.

The Besu client team advocated exploring a targeted revision to EIP-8037 to preserve existing smart contract behavior.

However, Ansgar Dietrichs and several other developers questioned whether a narrow adjustment would resolve enough problems to justify additional testing and development delays.

Marius van der Wijden also warned that changing how gas refunds are handled could disrupt contracts that depend on receiving those refunds during transaction execution.

The disagreement leaves developers choosing between allowing affected applications time to adjust to the existing specifications and redesigning parts of the upgrade to preserve more of their current behavior.

The Ethereum Foundation, alongside security researchers, has contacted more than 50 affected companies. During the meeting, Rahul reported that high-impact projects had completed or were expected to complete fixes by mid-December.

According to recent reports, other affected projects reported remediation schedules extending to Jan. 10, making mid-January the earliest viable mainnet activation window without specification changes.

A late-January or early-February rollout was also discussed as a more realistic possibility.

However, Dietrichs outlined substantially longer timelines if developers postpone their decision to investigate alternative rules.

According to recent reports, waiting until January to decide whether to retain the existing specifications could push activation into late February or early March. Adopting specification changes then could extend the rollout to April or May.

Such delays would also affect Ethereum's broader upgrade schedule, including preparations for Hegotá, which developers are discussing in connection with the network's post-quantum security transition.

The competing priorities have strengthened support for maintaining Glamsterdam's current design.

Developers are now considering a Hoodi activation around Dec. 16 or 17, after an earlier October test was postponed over compatibility concerns.

Sources indicate that the Nov. 19 call summary maps the decisions ahead for Glamsterdam, Ethereum’s next upgrade.

The proposed gas rules give app teams a working baseline while developers consider revisions.

Hoodi is a public testnet. Mainnet activation timing remains open.

Map the call summary's proposed decision and test window alongside the Ethereum Foundation's app compatibility guidance and prior Sepolia simulation reporting.

Sources indicate that hoodi is a public testnet. Mainnet activation timing remains open.

A final decision is expected during the next All Core Developers Consensus call on Nov. 26, when execution and consensus teams will determine whether to proceed with the December test.

Developers advocating changes have been asked to present specific alternatives, supported by impact analysis and auditor feedback, before that meeting.

Approval of the Hoodi schedule would effectively commit Ethereum to testing Glamsterdam's existing rules, leaving affected application teams to complete their fixes before the upgrade reaches mainnet.

Institutions are Piling Into Bitcoin ETFs, Pushing Holdings to a Record

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • spot bitcoin exchange-traded products as net buyers in the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record 356,491 BTC, according to a latest report from Galaxy Research.
  • Investment managers that file Form 13F with the SEC added the equivalent o f 49,229 BTC, net of sales, between July 1 and Sept.
  • Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, published the analysis Thursday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Institutions returned to U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded products as net buyers in the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record 356,491 BTC, according to a latest report from Galaxy Research.

Investment managers that file Form 13F with the SEC added the equivalent o f 49,229 BTC, net of sales, between July 1 and Sept. 30. That is the most since the second quarter of 2025 and more than the 47,054 BTC they sold over the previous three quarters. The holdings were worth $29.78 billion at quarter-end prices.

Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, published the analysis Thursday. The buying came as bitcoin swung between a bear-market low of $57,717 on July 1 and a high of $87,397 on Sept. 21, and Galaxy remarked the accumulation continued through that range.

Sources indicate that half of the net addition came from advisors and wealth platforms, a group that includes registered investment advisors, wealth managers, wirehouses and broker-dealer platforms. The category reported 144,307 BTC, or 40.5% of all 13F-reported holdings, the highest share since the funds launched in January 2024.

It has been revealed that those firms have now been net buyers for nine straight quarters. Their holdings are 3.3 times their March 2024 level, and Galaxy mentioned the group accounts for 100,003 of the 179,300 BTC that all filers have added since the second quarter of 2024.

It has been revealed that wirehouses drove the quarter. The category added a record 24,838 BTC, led by Wells Fargo at 14,636 BTC, Bank of America at 7,201 BTC and Morgan Stanley at 2,875 BTC.

Wells Fargo became the largest 13F holder for the first time. It reported 30,553 BTC, worth $2.55 billion, nearly double the 15,931 BTC it held on June 30, and passed Jane Street. No wealth platform had ranked first before, and Millennium Management had held the top spot in every quarter from early 2024 through the first quarter of 2026.

In a recent development, hedge funds now hold 19.0% of 13F-reported holdings, down from 50.6% at the end of 2024. Basis and relative-value funds hold 34,053 BTC, far below their peak of 101,826 BTC, though they and macro funds were both buyers last quarter, adding 9,184 BTC and 10,492 BTC.

Industry observers note that blackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounts for two-thirds of the institutional position. Filers hold 232,453 BTC in the fund, or 65.2% of everything reported, and IBIT took 34,744 BTC of the quarter’s net 49,229 BTC.

Filers’ holdings of Grayscale’s GBTC fell for the 10th straight quarter, and the lower-fee Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust passed it for the first time. The number of managers holding a spot bitcoin fund rose by 191 to 2,166, the first increase after two quarters of decline.

Recent findings suggest that galaxy noted that a few large firms drove the gain. The 50 largest holders added a net 59,578 BTC, while all other managers combined were net sellers of 10,349 BTC. Form 13F filers hold 27.6% of the bitcoin in the funds, up from 24.8% on June 30.

The filings describe Sept. 30, and the picture has changed since. Galaxy mentioned the funds’ bitcoin holdings have fallen by 38,531 BTC to 1,252,139 BTC as of Nov. 16, while the price of bitcoin dropped to $64,943 from $83,580. Bitcoin had traded above $81,500 as recently as Oct. 28.

Sources indicate that A Form 13F covers only long positions at quarter-end and only accounts over which the manager has investment discretion. Short positions and most derivatives are not reported, so shares held by a market maker or basis fund may be hedged. Galaxy also believes client-directed brokerage accounts leave wealth-channel ownership understated.

How filers behaved during the recent decline will not be known until the next round of filings arrives in February.

#6175. Tech Report: Tesla’s China sales crash 66% to lowest level in over four years

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1195 w)

Tech Report: Tesla’s China sales crash 66% to lowest level in over four years

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1195 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, only 8,817 of the cars Tesla delivered from Giga Shanghai in October went to Chinese buyers.
  • Industry observers note that back in July 2022, the Shanghai factory was partly shut down for line upgrades.
  • According to recent reports, the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) reported that Tesla China wholesaled 67,829 vehicles in October, up 10.3% year-over-year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, only 8,817 of the cars Tesla delivered from Giga Shanghai in October went to Chinese buyers. That’s down 66% from a year ago and Tesla’s worst month in China since July 2022, according to CPCA data.

Industry observers note that back in July 2022, the Shanghai factory was partly shut down for line upgrades. This time it ran normally and shipped 87% of what it built out of the country.

According to recent reports, the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) reported that Tesla China wholesaled 67,829 vehicles in October, up 10.3% year-over-year. That’s the number most headlines ran with.

Industry observers note that but 59,012 of those were exports. Strip them out and you’re left with 8,817 cars for the domestic market, the one Giga Shanghai was originally built to serve.

It has been revealed that nearly all of them were Model Ys (7,807), according to CnEVPost, leaving just 1,010 Model 3s. And compared to September, when Tesla sold 64,837 cars in China, domestic sales fell 86%.

Here’s how October has looked over the last three years:.

Tesla favors export orders early in each quarter and pushes domestic deliveries toward the end of it, and September’s promotions and quarter-end rush pulled some demand forward.

That’s real. Tesla’s China sales have followed this sawtooth pattern for years. Last October was also weak, and Tesla then delivered 73,145 cars in China in November and 93,843 in December.

Sources indicate that but it doesn’t explain the size of this drop. Here’s every first month of a quarter in 2026:.

Industry observers note that october is less than half of the previous low this year. And the October trough keeps getting deeper: 40,485 in 2024, 26,006 in 2025, 8,817 now.

Industry observers note that china’s EV market is having a rough year. NEV retail sales fell 10% year-over-year in October to 1.148 million units, according to CPCA’s preliminary data, as Beijing phases out trade-in subsidies and the NEV purchase tax exemption was cut in half on January 1. The overall passenger car market was down 25%.

In a recent development, tesla was down 66%. That works out to about 0.8% of China’s NEV retail market last month.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Xiaomi, which only started delivering cars in 2024, delivered more than 50,000 vehicles in October. Leapmotor delivered 106,127, up 51%. BYD delivered 490,168, though that includes its exports.

Through October, Tesla has sold 389,905 cars in China. That’s down 15% from 458,710 over the same period last year and its lowest January-to-October total in at least four years:.

Recent findings suggest that the decline is speeding up. Tesla was down 11.9% in China through September, and one bad October pushed that to 15%. This year is now 22% below the 2024 peak, or about 110,000 fewer cars.

Exports from Giga Shanghai went the other way, up 101% to 420,984.

It has been revealed that so this year, Shanghai has now shipped more cars abroad than it sold at home. Last year, domestic sales beat exports by more than two to one.

Recent findings suggest that as we reported last month, Beijing is cutting the VAT export rebate on EVs from 13% to 9% on April 1, 2027, with the rate set by the customs declaration date. We said to expect automakers to cram exports in ahead of the deadline. October’s 59,012 exports, up 66% year-over-year, fit that.

According to recent reports, we’ve been tracking this gap all year, from Tesla’s Q1 China retail crash to the first-half numbers. Every time, the wholesale headline looks fine and the domestic number underneath gets worse. October is the most extreme version yet: Tesla China “grew” 10% while Chinese buyers bought 66% fewer Teslas.

Recent findings suggest that we don’t buy that this is just the quarterly cycle. The cycle explains why October is weaker than September. It doesn’t explain why this October is a third of last October, or less than half of any other month this year.

It has been revealed that I've been saying this for the last two years. Tesla's problem isn't that Elon temporarily alienated customers in Europe or other countries. Yes that killed sales for a bit, but in the end people are practical and will buy the best car for the money. And we saw that is exactly what happened with European Tesla sales coming back when gas prices rose and Tesla as a package (quality + price) was still very competitive.

The real problem that Tesla has is that they're falling behind in China not because anyone cares about Elon's politics, but because the cars are just less and less competitive. And while the Chinese competition doubles down on vehicle development and rolls out a new car every week, Tesla has lost all interest in it. There is absolutely nothing on the horizon for them in terms of new vehicles that consumers can buy. Looks like the 3 and Y are all they will have and no updates are coming.

I know, FSD or bust, but that's also assuming Chinese brands don't crack that nut at the same time.

In a recent development, two things can be true at once. The export numbers show Tesla front-loading shipments ahead of the rebate cut. And Chinese demand for a Model 3 and Model Y lineup that hasn’t fundamentally changed in years keeps fading while Xiaomi, Leapmotor and BYD launch fresh models every few months.

And if Tesla is choosing to send cars abroad instead of selling them in China, that’s not exactly a vote of confidence in its Chinese business either.

The real test is November and December. Last year, Tesla bounced back to 73,000 and 94,000 domestic sales. If it gets close to that again, October was mostly timing. If it doesn’t, Tesla has a serious problem in the world’s largest EV market, and the export valve that’s been hiding it gets more expensive in April.

Shiba Inu’s layer-2 network, Shibarium, is experiencing a major slowdown as daily network activity has fallen to three-digit figures (fewer than 1,000 transactions), hitting lows not seen in months.

Sources indicate that shibarium processed 546 transactions, according to Shibariumscan data, marking a slower period for the layer-2 network after activity spiked to a high of 6,370 on October 31, 2026. Transaction activity declined afterward, and the decline intensified amid the sell-off that hit the market in recent weeks.

Recent findings suggest that the latest figures suggest that fewer transactions are taking place across Shibarium compared with periods of stronger activity. The key question now is whether Shibarium can regain momentum in the coming weeks.

Meanwhile, development continues behind the scenes for the Shiba Inu layer-2 network, as long-time Shiba Inu community member and developer Mazrael revealed a big batch of contracts deployed on Puppynet, Shibarium's testnet.

But in the meantime, Shibarium’s fall to three-digit activity levels is a major slowdown that SHIB holders and ecosystem watchers will be watching closely.

Shiba Inu's on-chain holders increased as the number of wallets holding SHIB hit 1,700,930 on November 19, 2026.

According to the latest figures shared by Etherscan SHIB, an X account dedicated to providing updates on the SHIB ecosystem, the cryptocurrency added 236 new on-chain holders in a single day, taking its total past the 1.7 million milestone.

Industry observers note that the month of November has also seen consistent growth, with SHIB adding 4,520 holders since the start of the month. The broader 2026 trend is even more pronounced, with the number of holders of the token increasing by 152,300 since the beginning of the year.

While Shiba Inu's latest milestone seems remarkable, Mazrael suggested that the Shib ecosystem, including Shibarium, might have more holders than indicated, with 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on the BNB Chain.

"Shibarium has more holders than those you listed, though. But yeah. Well, there are also 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on BNB. But that's not actually CCIP SHIB; it is a peg," Mazrael wrote.

#6172. The Customer Loyalty Secret? It’s Not Just About Shopping
